sentences.zh: 唐受命二百八十八年，以孝悌名通朝廷者，多閭巷刺草之民，皆得書於史官。

translations.literal: The Tang received the Mandate for two hundred eighty-eight years; those whose names for filial piety and brotherly duty reached the court were mostly common people of alleys and lanes who gathered medicinal herbs, and all were recorded by the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Over the two hundred eighty-eight years of Tang rule, those famed at court for filial piety and brotherly devotion were largely humble folk from back lanes who pricked and collected herbs—yet all earned a place in the official histories.

sentences.zh: 萬年王世貴，長安嚴待封，涇陽田伯明，華原韓難陀，華州王瞿曇，鄭縣辛法汪、郭士舉、張長、郭士度、鄭迪、柳仁忠、能君德、劉崇、甘元爽、韓子尚、韓思約，下邽張萬徹，朝邑申屠思恭、呂昂，鶉觚張元亮，靈臺孫智和，新平馮猛將，宜川司馬芬，洛交周崇俊，洛川何善宜，博陵崔定仁，冀州燕遺倩，貝州馬衡，滄州鄭士才，清池孫楚信、劉賢，渤海邊鳳舉，瀛州朱寶積，樂陵蘇伏念，邯鄲章征，雞澤馮仁海、郭守素，文安董相，武邑王達多、張丘感、張藝朗暨孫師才、張義節，沙河趙君惠，南樂谷感德，魏縣毛仁，武城茹智達，歷亭王師威、李肆仁，臨河李文綢，湯陰後斥奴，鼓城彭思義、陳屺、田堤嶽，太原盧遺仁、王知道，蒲州賈孝才，解縣衛玄表，南嶽張利見，安邑曹文行、孫懷應、相裏誌降、楊王操、邵玄同、張衡、曹存勛、李文褒、董文海、李文秀、張仙兒、張公憲，虞鄉董敬直，河東張金城、呂神通、呂雲、呂誌挺、呂元光、趙舉、張祐、姚熾、張師德、馮巨源、杜山藏，河西郭文政，伊闕任仲濟、源榮璧，汴州張士巖，陳留家師諒、董允恭，尉氏楊思貞，中牟潘良瑗暨子季通，陽武時惠珣，封丘楊嵩珪，許田李頤道，胙城蔡洪、石善雄暨孫彥威，朗山胡君才，徐州皇甫恒，彭城尹務榮，荊州劉寶，長壽史摶，益州焦懷肅、郭景華，郪縣曹少微，涪城趙煙，資陽趙光寓、黃，梓潼馬冬王、秦舉、王興嗣，依政樊漪，巴西韋士宗、文博熒暨子詮，南鄭李貞古，巢縣張進昭，萬載廖洪，南陵蘇仲方，鄱陽張讃，樂平謝惟勤、沈普、姜居，上饒鮑嘉福、虞熔真，句容張常洧，弋陽張球、李營暨子凝孫楚，貴溪黃舟，建昌熊士贍，臨江袁鳴，贛縣謝俊，餘杭何公弁、章成緬、方宗，建德何起門，桐廬祝希進，諸暨張萬和，蕭山李渭、許伯會、戴恭、俞僅，信安徐知新、徐惠諲，東陽應先、唐君祐，睦州許利川，建陽劉常，邵武黃亙、張巨篯、吳海，泉山黃嘉猷，永泰王奭，皆事親居喪著至行者。

sentences.zh: 萬年宋興貴，奉先張郛，澧陽張仁興，櫟陽董思寵，湖城閻旻，高平雍仙高，湖城閻酆，正平周思藝、張子英，曲沃張君密、秦德方、馬玄操、李君則，太平趙德儼，隴西陳嗣，北海呂元簡，經城宋洸之，單父劉九江，無棣徐文亮，樂陵吳正表，河間劉宣、董永，安邑任君義、衛開，龍門梁神義、賀見涉、張奇異，鄭縣王元緒、寇元童，舒城徐行周，睦州方良琨，桐廬戴元益，高安宋練，涇縣萬晏，弋陽李植，繁昌王丕，皆數世同居者。

translations.literal: Song Xinggui of Wannian, Zhang Kuo of Fengxian, Zhang Renxing of Liyang, Dong Sichong of Yueyang, Yan Min of Hucheng, Yong Xiangao of Gaoping, Yan Feng of Hucheng, Zhou Siyi and Zhang Ziying of Zhengping, Zhang Junmi, Qin Defang, Ma Xuancao, and Li Junze of Quwo, Zhao Deyan of Taiping, Chen Si of Longxi, Lü Yuanjian of Beihai, Song Guangzhi of Jingcheng, Liu Jiujiang of Shanfu, Xu Wenliang of Wudi, Wu Zhengbiao of Leling, Liu Xuan and Dong Yong of Hejian, Ren Junyi and Wei Kai of Anyi, Liang Shenyi, He Jianshe, and Zhang Qiyi of Longmen, Wang Yuanxu and Kou Yuantong of Zheng County, Xu Xingzhou of Shucheng, Fang Liangkun of Muzhou, Dai Yuanyi of Tonglu, Song Lian of Gao'an, Wan Yan of Jingxian, Li Zhi of Yiyang, and Wang Pi of Fanchang—all were those dwelling in common through several generations.

sentences.zh: 天子皆旌表門閭，賜粟帛，州縣存問，復賦稅，有授以官者。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven in every case erected commendatory markers at their gates and lanes, bestowed grain and silks, had prefectures and counties send inquiries to attend to them, remitted levies and taxes, and some were even invested with office.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the throne publicly honored their households at gate and lane, granted grain and cloth, had local officials look in on them, exempted them from taxes, and in some instances even appointed them to office.

sentences.zh: 唐時陳藏器著《本草拾遺》，謂人肉治羸疾，自是民間以父母疾，多刲股肉而進。

translations.literal: In Tang times Chen Cangqi compiled Supplement to the Materia Medica, stating that human flesh treats wasting illness; from then on among the people, when parents fell ill, many cut flesh from their thighs to present.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang, Chen Cangqi wrote Supplement to the Materia Medica and claimed that human flesh could cure emaciating disease; thereafter, whenever parents were sick, people commonly gouged flesh from their own thighs to feed them.

sentences.zh: 又有京兆張阿九、趙言，奉天趙正言、滑清泌，羽林飛騎啖榮祿，鄭縣吳孝友，華陰尹義華，潞州張光玼，解縣南鍛，河東李忠孝、韓放，鄢陵任客奴，絳縣張子英，平原楊仙朝，樂工段日升，河東將陳涉，襄陽馮子，城固雍孫八，虞鄉張抱玉、骨英秀，榆次馮秀誠，封丘楊嵩珪、劉浩，清池朱庭玉、弟庭金，繁昌朱忄存，歙縣黃芮，左千牛薛鋒及河陽劉士約，或給帛，或旌表門閭，皆名在國史。

translations.literal: There were also Zhang Ajiu and Zhao Yan of Jingzhao, Zhao Zhengyan of Fengtian, Hua Qingbi, the Yulin flying cavalryman Tan Ronglu, Wu Xiaoyou of Zheng County, Yin Yihua of Huayin, Zhang Guangci of Luzhou, Nan Duan of Jie County, Li Zhongxiao and Han Fang of Hedong, Ren Kenü of Yanling, Zhang Ziying of Jiang County, Yang Xianchao of Pingyuan, the musician Duan Risheng, the Hedong general Chen She, Feng Zi of Xiangyang, Yong Sunba of Chenggu, Zhang Baoyu and Gu Yingxiu of Yuxiang, Feng Xiucheng of Yuci, Yang Songgui and Liu Hao of Fengqiu, Zhu Tingyu and his younger brother Tingjin of Qingchi, Zhu Cun of Fanchang, Huang Rui of She County, the Left Thousand-Bull Cavalryman Xue Feng, and Liu Shiyue of Heyang; some received cloth allotments, some had their gates and lanes commended—all their names appear in the national histories.
translations.idiomatic: The annals also record filial exemplars from across the empire: Zhang Ajiu and Zhao Yan of the capital region, Zhao Zhengyan of Fengtian, the Yulin guardsman Tan Ronglu, Wu Xiaoyou of Zheng County, Yin Yihua of Huayin, Zhang Guangci of Luzhou, Nan Duan of Jie County, Li Zhongxiao and Han Fang of Hedong, Ren Kenü of Yanling, Zhang Ziying of Jiang County, Yang Xianchao of Pingyuan, the musician Duan Risheng, the Hedong general Chen She, Feng Zi of Xiangyang, Yong Sunba of Chenggu, Zhang Baoyu and Gu Yingxiu of Yuxiang, Feng Xiucheng of Yuci, Yang Songgui and Liu Hao of Fengqiu, Zhu Tingyu and his brother Tingjin of Qingchi, Zhu Cun of Fanchang, Huang Rui of She County, the Left Thousand-Bull Cavalryman Xue Feng, and Liu Shiyue of Heyang; some were rewarded with silks, others had their homes publicly honored, and every one of them earned a place in the state's official record.

sentences.zh: 善乎！

translations.literal: Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Admirable indeed!

sentences.zh: 韓愈之論也，曰：「父母疾，亨藥餌，以是為孝，未聞毀支體者也。

translations.literal: Han Yu's discourse says: "When parents are ill, one boils medicines and medicaments—taking this as filial piety; one has not heard of damaging the limbs.
translations.idiomatic: As Han Yu argued: "When one's parents fall ill, one prepares medicines and tonics—that is filial duty; I have never heard that mutilating one's body counts as filial.

sentences.zh: 茍不傷義，則聖賢先眾而為之。

translations.literal: If it did not harm righteousness, then sages and worthies would have done it before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: If such acts did not violate moral principle, the sages would long since have led the common people in doing them.

sentences.zh: 是不幸因而且死，則毀傷滅絕之罪有歸矣，安可旌其門以表異之？」

translations.literal: If by misfortune one moreover dies from it, then the guilt of destroying and injuring, extinguishing and cutting off, has its attribution; how could one commend their gate to mark them as extraordinary?"
translations.idiomatic: And if, through mischance, one dies of the wound, the guilt of self-mutilation and the extinguishing of one's line falls squarely upon that person—how then could the court honor their household as a model of excellence?

sentences.zh: 雖然，委巷之陋，非有學術禮義之資，能忘身以及其親，出於誠心，亦足稱者。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, the crudeness of alleys and lanes, lacking the resources of learning and ritual propriety, yet able to forget the self and extend to their kin, proceeding from sincere heart, is also sufficient to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Still, though these were humble folk of narrow lanes, without the cultivation of learning or ritual, anyone who could forget self for the sake of kin—and do so with genuine devotion—deserved commendation all the same.

sentences.zh: 故列十七八焉。

translations.literal: Therefore about seventeen or eighteen are listed here.
translations.idiomatic: Hence roughly a score of such cases are recorded below.

sentences.zh: 廣明後，方鎮淩法，誇地千里，事不上聞，孝悌篤行之士，旌命所不及。

translations.literal: After the Guangming era, frontier commanders overawed the law, boasting domains of a thousand li, affairs not reported upward; men of devoted filial piety and brotherliness did not reach where commendation edicts extended.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangming reign, military governors trampled the law and ruled vast domains as petty kingdoms; word of worthy deeds no longer reached the throne, and even the most devoted sons of filial piety lay beyond the reach of imperial reward.

sentences.zh: 載小說者，名字不參見他書，不可錄。

translations.literal: Those recorded in fiction, their names not cross-seen in other books, cannot be entered.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts drawn from popular tales, whose names cannot be verified in other sources, have been left out.

sentences.zh: 若李知本、張誌寬之屬，承上順下，有禮讓君子之風，故輯而序之。

translations.literal: Such as Li Zhiben, Zhang Zhikuan and their kind, receiving those above and yielding to those below, having the air of courteous and yielding gentlemen, therefore are gathered and arranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Li Zhiben and Zhang Zhikuan, who deferred to superiors and yielded to inferiors in the manner of true gentlemen, have been collected and set down in sequence.

sentences.zh: 張士巖父病，藥須鯉魚，冬月冰合，有獺銜魚至前，得以供父，父遂愈。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiyan's father was ill; the medicine required carp; in winter months ice congealed; an otter held a fish in its mouth and came before him; he was thereby able to supply his father, and his father then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shiyan's father fell ill, his remedy called for carp, but winter had sealed the waters with ice—until an otter swam up bearing a fish in its jaws. Zhang fed it to his father, who recovered.

sentences.zh: 母病癰，士巖吮血。

translations.literal: His mother suffered a carbuncle; Shiyan sucked the blood.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother developed a festering sore, Shiyan drew out the pus and blood with his mouth.

sentences.zh: 父亡，廬墓，有虎狼依之。

translations.literal: His father died; he dwelt in a hut at the grave; there were tigers and wolves that drew near to him.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he kept mourning watch at the tomb, and tigers and wolves came to nestle beside him.

sentences.zh: 焦懷肅母病，每嘗其唾，若味異，輒悲號幾絕。

translations.literal: Jiao Huaisu's mother was ill; each time he tasted her spittle; if the flavor was strange, he would then wail in grief nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao Huaisu's mother fell ill, he tasted her saliva each day; whenever the flavor seemed wrong, he would sob until he nearly fainted.

sentences.zh: 母終，水漿不入口五日，負土成墳，廬守，日一食，杖然後起。

translations.literal: When his mother ended, water and gruel did not enter his mouth for five days; he carried earth to form the mound; he kept hut and guard; one meal per day; only with a staff did he then rise.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he took neither food nor drink for five days, carried earth to build her tomb, and kept vigil beside it—eating once a day and rising only with the aid of a staff.

sentences.zh: 繼母沒，亦如之。

translations.literal: When his stepmother passed, he likewise did the same.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he observed the same rites.

sentences.zh: 張進昭，母患狐刺，左手墮而終。

translations.literal: Zhang Jinzhao—his mother suffered fox-sting; her left hand fell off and she ended.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinzhao's mother contracted a wasting disease of the hand known as "fox barb"; her left hand withered away before she died.

sentences.zh: 及殯，進昭截左腕廬於墓。

translations.literal: When it came to encoffining, Jinzhao cut off his left wrist and kept a hut at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: At her burial Zhang Jinzhao severed his own left wrist and maintained a mourning hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 張公藝九世同居，北齊東安王永樂、隋大使梁子恭躬慰撫，表其門。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongyi—nine generations dwelt together; Northern Qi Eastern An Prince Wang Yongle, Sui emissary Liang Zigong personally comforted and soothed, and commended his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongyi's clan lived under one roof for nine generations; the Eastern An prince Wang Yongle of Northern Qi and the Sui envoy Liang Zigong both came in person to console them and had their gate publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 高宗有事太山，臨幸其居，問本末，書「忍」字以對，天子為流涕，賜縑帛而去。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had business at Mount Tai; he visited his dwelling; asked beginning and end; wrote the character "forbearance" to reply; the Son of Heaven wept tears, bestowed silk and cloth, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong performed the Feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, he called at Zhang's home, asked how his family had endured together so long, and Zhang answered by writing a single character—"forbearance" (ren). The emperor wept, rewarded him with silks, and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 四人名頗著，詳見於篇。

translations.literal: The four men's names are rather renowned; details are fully seen in the chapters.
translations.idiomatic: These four men were already well known; fuller accounts appear in the sections below.

sentences.zh: 李知本，趙州元氏人，元魏洛州刺史靈六世孫。

translations.literal: Li Zhiben, a man of Yuanshi in Zhao prefecture, sixth-generation descendant of Ling, Luozhou governor of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhiben was a native of Yuanshi in Zhao Prefecture and a sixth-generation descendant of Ling, who had served as governor of Luozhou under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父孝端，仕隋為獲嘉丞。

translations.literal: His father Xiaoduan served the Sui as Huojia magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Xiaoduan held office under the Sui as magistrate of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 與族弟太沖俱有世閥，而太沖官婚最高，鄉人語曰：「太沖無兄，孝端無弟。」

translations.literal: With his clansman younger cousin Taichong he both had hereditary pedigrees, yet Taichong's office and marriage were highest; village people said: "Taichong has no elder brother, Xiaoduan has no younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: He and his clansman Taichong both came from eminent families, but Taichong outranked him in office and marriage; the villagers joked, "Taichong has no elder brother, and Xiaoduan has no younger brother."

sentences.zh: 知本涉經術，事親篤至，與弟知隱雍順，子孫百餘，至貲用僮仆無間也。

translations.literal: Zhiben crossed into classical studies; serving kin was devoted to the utmost; with his younger brother Zhiyin he was harmonious and obedient; descendants were over a hundred; even to goods, use, and servants there was no division.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiben was versed in the classics and utterly devoted in serving his parents; with his brother Zhiyin he lived in perfect harmony. Their descendants numbered more than a hundred, who shared wealth, provisions, and servants without distinction.

sentences.zh: 大業末，盜賊過閭不入，相戒曰：「無犯義門。」

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, when bandits passed through the lane they did not enter, and warned one another, saying, "Do not violate the Gate of Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Daye, raiders would pass the neighborhood yet never step inside, warning each other: "Don't touch the Gate of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 往依者五百餘室，皆以免。

translations.literal: More than five hundred households that came to rely on them all escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of the five hundred-odd households that sought shelter there was spared.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，知隱為伊闕丞，知本夏津令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Zhi Yin served as magistrate of Yique, and Zhi Ben as magistrate of Xiajin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Zhi Yin became magistrate of Yique and Zhi Ben magistrate of Xiajin.

sentences.zh: 開元中，孫瑱為給事中、揚州長史。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period, his grandson Zhen served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, his grandson Zhen rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知隱孫颙，有文辭，至太常少卿。

translations.literal: Zhi Yin's grandson Yong had literary talent and reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yin's grandson Yong, a gifted writer, eventually became vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從祖兄弟位給事中，凡四人。

translations.literal: Cousins on his father's side who held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary numbered four in all.
translations.idiomatic: Four of his father's cousins altogether served as attendants-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 張誌寬，蒲州安邑人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhikuan was a man of Anyi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhikuan came from Anyi in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居父喪而毀，州裏稱之。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his father he emaciated himself through grief, and the district praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He wasted away in grief during his father's mourning, and the whole district spoke of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 王君廓兵略地，不暴其閭，倚全者百許姓。

translations.literal: When Wang Junkuo's troops seized territory, they did not ravage his neighborhood; about a hundred surnames who relied on him were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junkuo's armies overran the countryside, yet left their lane untouched—nearly a hundred clans who sheltered with them survived unscathed.

sentences.zh: 後為裏正，忽詣縣稱母疾求急，令問狀，對曰：「母有疾，誌寬輒病，是以知之。」

translations.literal: Later, as hamlet chief, he suddenly went to the county and claimed his mother was ill and begged urgent leave; the magistrate asked the facts, and he replied, "When my mother is ill, Zhikuan at once falls ill—therefore I know it."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as village head, he rushed to the county office claiming his mother was gravely ill and pleading to be sent home at once. When the magistrate pressed him, he said, "Whenever my mother sickens, I sicken too—that is how I know.

sentences.zh: 令謂其妄，系於獄，馳驗如言，乃慰遣之。

translations.literal: The magistrate called it falsehood and imprisoned him, but sent runners to verify; it was as he had said, and he was comforted and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate judged him a liar and threw him in jail, then dispatched messengers to check—and found it exactly so. Only then was he consoled and released.

sentences.zh: 母終，負土成墳，手蒔松柏。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to form the mound and with his own hands planted pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he piled the grave with his own labor and planted every pine and cypress himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使者就吊，拜員外散騎常侍，賜物四十段，表其閭。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent envoys to offer condolences on the spot, appointed him Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary, bestowed forty lengths of goods, and had his lane commended.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu dispatched envoys to mourn him in person, named him extraordinary attendant-in-ordinary, granted forty bolts of goods, and ordered his neighborhood honored with an imperial plaque.

sentences.zh: 劉君良，瀛州饒陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Junliang was a man of Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Junliang came from Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四世同居，族兄弟猶同產也，門內鬥粟尺帛無所私。

translations.literal: Four generations lived under one roof; even clan cousins were like children of the same womb, and within the gates not a peck of grain or foot of cloth was kept private.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations dwelt together; cousins behaved like full brothers, and under their roof not a single peck of grain or span of cloth was held back for oneself alone.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，荒饉，妻勸其異居，因易置庭樹鳥雛，令鬥且鳴，家人怪之，妻曰：「天下亂，禽鳥不相容，況人邪！」

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in the Sui, when famine struck, his wife urged them to live apart; she therefore switched the chicks in the courtyard tree nests, made the birds fight and cry out, and when the household wondered at it she said, "The realm is in chaos—even birds cannot tolerate one another, how much less men!"
translations.idiomatic: In the great famine at the close of Sui Daye, his wife pressed for separate households. She secretly swapped the nestlings in the courtyard trees until the birds were fighting and shrieking. When the family marveled, she said, "The world is falling apart—if birds cannot share a branch, what hope is there for men?

sentences.zh: 君良即與兄弟別處。

translations.literal: Junliang at once went to live apart from his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Junliang yielded at once and moved out with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 月餘，密知其計，因斥去妻，曰：「爾破吾家！」

translations.literal: After more than a month he secretly learned her scheme, and therefore drove out his wife, saying, "You have broken my family!"
translations.idiomatic: A month later he saw through her plot, cast her out, and cried, "You have ruined our house!

sentences.zh: 召兄弟流涕以告，更復同居。

translations.literal: He summoned his brothers, weeping as he told them, and they again lived together.
translations.idiomatic: He called his brothers back, told them through tears what had happened, and they took up common life once more.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，鄉人共依之，眾築為堡，因號義成堡。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos, fellow villagers all relied on him; the multitude built a fort and therefore called it Fort of Righteous Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire unraveled, neighbors flocked to him; hundreds banded together into a walled refuge they named Fort of Righteous Accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 武德中，深州別駕楊弘業至其居，凡六院共一庖，子弟皆有禮節，嘆挹而去。

translations.literal: In the Wude period, Yang Hongye, vice-prefect of Shen Prefecture, came to his residence; in all six courtyards shared one kitchen, and the sons and younger brothers all had ritual propriety; he sighed in admiration and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, Shen Prefecture's vice-prefect Yang Hongye visited his home. Six courtyards cooked from a single hearth; every son and nephew showed flawless courtesy. Hongye left sighing in wonder.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，表異門閭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, a memorial was submitted commending his exceptional gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 his household was formally commended for its extraordinary unity.

sentences.zh: 王少玄，博州聊城人。

translations.literal: Wang Shaoxuan was a man of Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaoxuan came from Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父隋末死亂兵，遺腹生少玄。

translations.literal: His father died among the rebel troops at the end of the Sui; Shaoxuan was born posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: His father was killed in the civil wars at the end of Sui; Shaoxuan was born after his death.

sentences.zh: 甫十歲，問父所在，母以告，即哀泣求屍。

translations.literal: When he had just turned ten, he asked where his father was; his mother told him, and he at once wept in grief and sought the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Barely ten, he asked where his father lay. When his mother told him, he broke into mourning wails and set out to find the body.

sentences.zh: 時野中白骨覆壓，或曰：「以子血漬而滲者，父胔也。」

translations.literal: At that time white bones lay heaped in the wilds, and some said, "Where a son's blood is applied and seeps in, that is the father's corpse."
translations.idiomatic: The fields were choked with anonymous bones. People said that if you smeared a bone with a son's blood and the blood sank in, you had found your father's remains.

sentences.zh: 少玄镵膚，閱旬而獲，遂以葬。

translations.literal: Shaoxuan scraped his skin, and within about ten days obtained it, and then buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxuan cut his flesh again and again. In ten days he found the right bones and buried his father.

sentences.zh: 創甚，彌年乃興。

translations.literal: His wounds were severe; only after a full year could he rise.
translations.idiomatic: The injuries were grave; a full year passed before he could stand again.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，州言狀，拜徐王府參軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan period the prefecture reported the facts, and he was appointed retainer on the staff of the Prince of Xu's household.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan the prefecture reported his story, and he was named a staff officer in the household of the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 任敬臣，字希古，棣州人。

translations.literal: Ren Jingchen, styled Xigu, was a man of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Jingchen, courtesy name Xigu, came from Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪母，哀毀天至。

translations.literal: At five he lost his mother and grieved with such extreme devastation that it reached heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at five and mourned with a child's grief so fierce it seemed to shake the sky.

sentences.zh: 七歲，問父英曰：「若何可以報母？」

translations.literal: At seven he asked his father Ying, "How may I repay my mother?"
translations.idiomatic: At seven he asked his father Ying, "What can I do to repay Mother?

sentences.zh: 英曰：「揚名顯親可也。」

translations.literal: Ying said, "To make your name known and bring honor to your kin will do."
translations.idiomatic: Ying answered, "Bring honor to the family and let your name be known—that is repayment enough."

sentences.zh: 乃刻誌從學。

translations.literal: He thereupon carved his resolve and followed his studies.
translations.idiomatic: He carved that vow into his heart and threw himself into learning.

sentences.zh: 汝南任處權見其文，驚曰：「孔子稱顏回之賢，以為弗如也。

translations.literal: Ren Chujian of Runan, seeing his writings, was startled and said, "Confucius praised Yan Hui's worth, holding that he himself could not match it.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Chujian of Runan read his essays and exclaimed, "Confucius praised Yan Hui and said he himself fell short—

sentences.zh: 吾非古人，然見此兒，信不可及。」

translations.literal: I am no man of antiquity, yet seeing this boy, I truly know he is beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: I am no sage of old, but meeting this boy I know I can never catch up to him.

sentences.zh: 十六，刺史崔樞欲舉秀才，自以學未廣，遁去。

translations.literal: At sixteen, Prefect Cui Shu wished to recommend him for Presented Scholar; he considered his learning not yet broad and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Prefect Cui Shu meant to nominate him as a presented scholar. Judging his learning still shallow, Jingchen slipped away.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒業，舉孝廉，授著作局正字。

translations.literal: After three more years he completed his course, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, and was appointed proofreader in the Bureau of Authorship.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he finished his studies, earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt, and received appointment as proofreader in the Bureau of Authorship.

sentences.zh: 父亡，數殞絕，繼母曰：「而不勝喪，謂孝可乎？」

translations.literal: When his father died he repeatedly fainted to the brink; his stepmother said, "You cannot bear up under mourning—can that be called filial?"
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death he collapsed again and again. His stepmother said, "If you cannot survive your mourning, what filial piety is that?

sentences.zh: 敬臣更進饘粥。

translations.literal: Jingchen again took gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen forced himself to take thin gruel once more.

sentences.zh: 服除，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was promoted to secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 休沐，闔門誦書。

translations.literal: On his days off he shut the door and recited books.
translations.idiomatic: On rest days he barred the gate and read aloud through the house.

sentences.zh: 監虞世南器其人，歲終，書上考，固辭。

translations.literal: Overseer Yu Shinan valued the man; at year's end he wrote the highest grade on his evaluation, but Jingchen firmly declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Yu Shinan admired him. At year's end Shinan marked him top of the roster; Jingchen refused the honor outright.

sentences.zh: 召為弘文館學士，俄授越王府西閣祭酒。

translations.literal: He was summoned as scholar of the Hongwen Hall, and soon appointed libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Prince of Yue's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the Hongwen Hall as a scholar, then soon made libationer of the Western Pavilion in the Prince of Yue's household.

sentences.zh: 當代，王再表留，進朝請郎。

translations.literal: In his own time the prince again memorialized to retain him, and he was advanced to gentleman for court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The prince repeatedly petitioned to keep him at court, and he rose to gentleman for court audiences.

sentences.zh: 舉制科，擢許王文學。

translations.literal: He passed the decree examination and was promoted to literary scholar for the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the decree examination and was appointed literary scholar to the household of the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 復為弘文館學士，終太子舍人。

translations.literal: Zhi Shucai was a man of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shucai came from Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 支叔才，定州人。

translations.literal: Zhi Shucai was a man of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shucai came from Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋末荒饉，夜丐食野中，還進母，為賊執，欲殺之，告以情，賊閔其孝，為解縛。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui there was famine and dearth; at night he begged food in the wilds, returned and presented it to his mother, was seized by bandits who meant to kill him; he told them the circumstances, the bandits pitied his filial devotion, and undid his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui dynasty collapsed into famine, he scavenged food in the fields by night and brought it home to his mother. Bandits seized him and were about to kill him; when he explained why he was out, they were moved by his devotion and let him go.

sentences.zh: 母病癰，叔才吮瘡註藥。

translations.literal: When his mother had a carbuncle, Shucai sucked the sore and poured in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His mother developed an abscess; he sucked the wound clean and applied the medicines himself.

sentences.zh: 及亡，廬墓，有白鵲止廬傍。

translations.literal: When she died, he built a mourning hut at the tomb; a white magpie came to rest beside the hut.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he kept vigil in a hut by the grave, and a white magpie alighted beside his shelter.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，表異其家。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, his household was entered in the register of exceptional conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, the court singled out his family for special honor.

sentences.zh: 至德間，有常州人王遇、弟遐俱為賊執，將釋一人，兄弟相讓死，賊感其意，盡縱之。

translations.literal: During the Zhide reign, two men of Changzhou, Wang Yu and his younger brother Xia, were both seized by bandits, who would release only one; the brothers each yielded death to the other, the bandits were moved by their intent, and released them both.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era, Wang Yu of Changzhou and his younger brother Xia were both taken by robbers, who said they would free only one. Each brother insisted the other should live; touched by their mutual sacrifice, the thieves set them both free.

sentences.zh: 程袁師，宋州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanshi was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanshi came from Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母病，十旬不褫帶，藥不嘗不進。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, for a hundred days he did not remove his belt; he would not present medicine he had not tasted.
translations.idiomatic: While his mother lay ill, he went a hundred days without loosening his clothes to sleep; no dose reached her lips until he had tasted it himself.

sentences.zh: 代弟戍洛州。

translations.literal: He took his younger brother's place on garrison duty at Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved his younger brother of military service at Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 母終，聞訃，日走二百里，因負土築墳，號臒，人不復識。

translations.literal: When his mother died and he heard the tidings, he ran two hundred li in a day; he carried earth to build the mound, cried until he was emaciated, and people could no longer recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his mother's death reached him, he covered two hundred li in a single day, then hauled earth to raise the grave. He wailed until he was wasted to skin and bone, and his own kin could scarcely tell who he was.

sentences.zh: 改葬曾門以來，閱二十年乃畢。

translations.literal: From the time he began reburying the graves of his forebears in the senior line, twenty years passed before the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The task of reburying his ancestors in the main lineage alone took him twenty years to complete.

sentences.zh: 常有白狼、黃蛇馴墓左，每哭，群鳥鳴翔。

translations.literal: White wolves and yellow serpents were often tame at the left of the tomb; whenever he wept, flocks of birds cried and wheeled.
translations.idiomatic: A white wolf and a yellow serpent would linger tamely to the left of the mound; whenever he broke into mourning cries, birds gathered overhead, calling and circling.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，刺史狀諸朝，詔吏敦駕。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui reign, the prefect memorialized him to the court, and an edict ordered officials to escort him in the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui, the prefect reported his case to the throne, and the emperor commanded officials to bring him to court with all due honor.

sentences.zh: 既至，不願仕，授儒林郎，還之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he did not wish to take office; he was given the title of Rulin Lang and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital he declined appointment; the court named him a Gentleman of the Forest of Scholars and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 武弘度，士兄之子，補相州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: Wu Hongdu, son of Shixiong, was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Justice Troops of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hongdu, son of Zhang Shiyan's elder brother Shixiong, was appointed assistant military registrar of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，父卒，自徐州被發徒跣趨喪所，負土築塋，晨夕號，日一溢米。

translations.literal: In Yonghui his father died; from Xuzhou, in hemp mourning dress and barefoot, he hurried to the funeral site, carried earth to build the grave mound, wailed morning and evening, and ate only one yi of rice a day.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui his father died. He set out from Xuzhou in mourning weeds, barefoot, and ran to the burial ground. There he heaped the grave with his own hands, keening day and night on a single cup of rice a day.

sentences.zh: 素芝產廬前，貍擾其旁。

translations.literal: White ganoderma grew before his mourning hut, and raccoon dogs frolicked beside it.
translations.idiomatic: White lingzhi sprang up before his tomb shelter, and tanuki sported peacefully at his side.

sentences.zh: 高宗下詔褒美，旌其門。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong issued an edict praising him and marked his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong issued a commendatory edict and had his household gate ceremonially honored.

sentences.zh: 宋思禮，字過庭，事繼母徐為聞孝。

translations.literal: Song Silu, courtesy name Guoting, in serving his stepmother Xu became famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Song Silu, styled Guoting, won wide renown for the devotion he showed his stepmother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 補蕭縣主簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of Xiaoxian County.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，井池涸，母羸疾，非泉水不適口，思禮憂懼且禱，忽有泉出諸庭，味甘寒，日不乏汲。

translations.literal: There came a great drought; wells and pools dried up; his mother was frail and ill and could take nothing but spring water; Silu was anxious and prayed; suddenly a spring issued forth in the courtyard, its taste sweet and cold, and each day there was no lack of water to draw.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought dried every well and pool. His mother, wasted by illness, could stomach only spring water. Silu prayed in dread—and a spring suddenly welled up in the courtyard, cool and sweet, never failing day after day.

sentences.zh: 縣人異之，尉柳晃為刻石頌其感。

translations.literal: The people of the county marveled at it; the assistant magistrate Liu Huang carved a stone to praise his moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The county was astonished; Assistant Magistrate Liu Huang had a stele cut to celebrate how Heaven had answered his grief.

sentences.zh: 鄭潛曜者，父萬鈞，駙馬都尉、滎陽郡公。

translations.literal: As for Zheng Qianyao: his father was Wan Jun, Commandant of the Empress's Sons-in-law and Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qianyao was the son of Wan Jun, Princess's consort and Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 母，代國長公主。

translations.literal: His mother was the Princess of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was the Princess of the Dai domain.

sentences.zh: 開元中，主寢疾，潛曜侍左右，造次不去，累三月不靧面。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan reign, when the princess lay ill, Qianyao attended at her left and right; in no hurried moment did he leave, and for three months together he did not rinse his face.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, as his mother grew sick, Qianyao kept constant vigil at her bedside, never stirring even for a moment, and for three full months he would not wash his face.

sentences.zh: 主疾侵，刺血為書請諸神，丐以身代。

translations.literal: When the princess's illness deepened, he pierced his flesh to draw blood and wrote a petition to the spirits, begging to substitute his own person for hers.
translations.idiomatic: As her condition worsened, he pricked his arm and wrote a blood-letter pleading with the gods to take his life in place of hers.

sentences.zh: 火書，而「神許」二字獨不化。

translations.literal: He burned the writing, yet the two characters "Divine Assent" alone did not transform.
translations.idiomatic: He set the letter to flame, but the words "Divine Assent" alone would not burn away.

sentences.zh: 翌日主愈，戒左右無敢言。

translations.literal: On the morrow the princess recovered; he warned those at her side that none might speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his mother was well again, and he forbade anyone in her household to breathe a word of what had happened.

sentences.zh: 後尚臨晉長公主，歷太仆光祿卿。

translations.literal: Later he took in marriage the Princess of Linjin, and served in succession as Grand Master of Studs and as Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He later married the Princess of Linjin and rose from Grand Master of Studs to Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 元讓，雍州武功人。

translations.literal: Yuan Rang was a man of Wugong in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rang came from Wugong in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，以母病不肯調，侍膳不出閭數十年。

translations.literal: He was advanced through the Mingjing examination, but because his mother was ill he would not accept appointment; he attended her meals and for several decades did not go beyond his lane.
translations.idiomatic: Though he passed the Mingjing examination, he refused office while his mother was sick and for decades never left the lane, tending her at every meal.

sentences.zh: 母終，廬墓次，廢櫛沐，飯菜飲水。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he dwelt in a hut beside the grave, abandoned combing and washing, and took only vegetables and water to eat and drink.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he lived in a mourning hut by the tomb, forgoing bath and grooming and subsisting on plain vegetables and water alone.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，太子監國，下令表闕於門。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng reign, while the crown prince supervised the state, an order was issued to erect a commemorative gate-marker at his door.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianheng, with the crown prince regent, the court ordered a filial-honor marker raised at his gate.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，巡察使表讓孝悌卓越，擢太子右內率府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchun, the touring inspector memorialized that Rang's filial piety and brotherly duty were outstanding, and he was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Right Inner Rate Palace of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yongchun an inspector reported his filial devotion as extraordinary, and he was appointed chief secretary in the crown prince's Right Inner Rate Palace.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，還鄉里，人有所訟，皆詣讓判。

translations.literal: When his term expired he returned to his native place; whenever people had lawsuits, all went to Rang to judge them.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he went home, and villagers with any dispute would bring it to Rang for judgment.

sentences.zh: 中宗在東宮，召拜司議郎，入謁，武後望謂曰：「卿孝於家，必能忠於國，宜以治道輔吾子。」

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, he was summoned and appointed Reviewer of Discussions; on entering audience, Empress Wu looked at him and said: "You are filial in the family—you will surely be loyal to the state. You should assist my son with the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhongzong was still heir apparent, Rang was summoned as palace reviewer. At his audience Empress Wu regarded him and said, "Filial at home, you will be loyal abroad—guide my son in the arts of rule.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 裴敬彜，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Jingyi was a man of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jingyi came from Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖子通，隋開皇中以太中大夫居母喪，哭喪明，有白烏巢冢樾。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zitong, in the Kaihuang reign of Sui as Grand Master for Palace Discourse, dwelt in mourning for his mother; he wept at the funeral until he went blind, and a white crow nested in the tree over the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zitong, a Grand Master for Palace Discourse under Sui Kaihuang, mourned his mother until weeping left him blind; a white crow nested in the tree above her grave.

sentences.zh: 兄弟八人皆為名孝，詔表門闕，世謂「義門裴氏」。

translations.literal: Eight brothers were all famed for filial piety; an edict marked their gate and tower, and the age called them the "Righteous Gate Pei Clan."
translations.idiomatic: All eight brothers won renown for filial devotion; the throne honored their gate, and men spoke of the "Righteous Gate Pei Clan."

sentences.zh: 敬彜七歲能文章，性謹敏，宗族重之，號「甘露頂」。

translations.literal: At seven years Jingyi could compose writings; his nature was careful and keen, and the clan prized him, calling him the "Sweet Dew Crown."
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi could already write at seven, and his careful, quick mind won the clan's esteem—they nicknamed him the "Sweet Dew Crown."

sentences.zh: 父智周，補臨黃令，為下所訟。

translations.literal: His father Zhizhou was appointed magistrate of Linhuang and was sued by subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhizhou served as magistrate of Linhuang until subordinates brought suit against him.

sentences.zh: 敬彜年十四，詣巡察使唐臨直枉，臨奇之，試命作賦，賦工。

translations.literal: When Jingyi was fourteen he went to the touring inspector Tang Lin to report a wrongful case; Lin marveled at him, tested him by ordering a fu composition, and the fu was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he sought out the inspector Tang Lin to protest his father's injustice. Tang was astonished, set him a fu to write, and the piece was masterly.

sentences.zh: 父罪已釋，表敬彜於朝，補陳王府典簽。

translations.literal: After his father's guilt had been released, he was memorialized to the court, and Jingyi was appointed Recorder of the Prince of Chen's household.
translations.idiomatic: Once his father was cleared, Jingyi was recommended to court and made recorder in the household of the Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽泣涕謂左右曰：「大人病痛，吾輒然，今心悸而痛，事叵測。」

translations.literal: One day he suddenly wept and told those beside him: "The elder is in pain and illness—I always feel it accordingly; now my heart palpitates and aches, and the matter cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: One day he burst into tears before his attendants: "When my father suffers, I feel it at once—now my heart pounds and aches, and I fear the worst.

sentences.zh: 乃請急，倍道歸，而父已卒，羸毀逾禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested urgent leave, returned by double stages, yet his father had already died; his emaciation in mourning exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He begged emergency leave and raced home, only to find his father already dead; his grief wasted him beyond what ritual prescribed.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，遷累監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng he was transferred and promoted cumulatively to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianfeng he rose through successive postings to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 母病，醫許仁則者鐍不能乘，敬彜自為輿往迎。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, the physician Xu Renze was lame and could not mount a carriage; Jingyi himself made a litter and went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's illness the physician Xu Renze was too crippled to ride; Jingyi built a sedan chair and went to fetch him on foot.

sentences.zh: 既居喪，詔贈縑帛，官為作靈輿。

translations.literal: Once he had entered mourning, an edict bestowed silks, and officials made a funeral carriage for him.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning the court granted him silks, and officials provided his funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 終服，以著作郎兼修國史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served as Author at the Palace Library, concurrently editing the National History.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he became a palace author and helped compile the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人、太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later held posts as secretariat drafting secretary and left subordinate to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 武後時，為酷吏所陷，死嶺南。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu he was framed by cruel officials and died in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, cruel officials destroyed him, and he died in exile in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 梁文貞，虢州閺鄉人。

translations.literal: Liang Wenzhen was a man of Minxiang in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wenzhen came from Minxiang in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從軍守邊，逮還，親已亡。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army to guard the frontier; when he returned at last, his kin were already dead.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army young and served on the frontier; by the time he came home, both parents were gone.

sentences.zh: 自傷不得養，即穿壙為門，晨夕汛掃，廬墓左，喑默三十年，家人有所問，畫文以對。

translations.literal: Grieving that he had not been able to nurture them, he bored through the tomb chamber as a door, morning and evening swept and rinsed, built a hut to the left of the grave, and was mute for thirty years; when his family had questions, he wrote characters to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken that he had never cared for them in life, he cut a doorway into the tomb vault, swept it morning and night, and lived in a hut beside the mound—silent for thirty years, answering kin only in written words.

sentences.zh: 會官改新道，出文貞廬前，行旅見之，皆為流涕。

translations.literal: It happened that officials altered the new road so that it issued before Wenzhen's hut; travelers who saw it all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When authorities rerouted the highway past his mourning hut, every traveler who passed wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 有甘露降塋木，白兔馴擾，縣令刊石紀之。

translations.literal: Sweet dew descended on the tomb-tree; a white rabbit grew tame and playful; the magistrate carved a stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew fell on the grave trees, a white rabbit lingered tamely about the mound, and the county magistrate had the marvels cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 開元中，刺史許景先表文貞孝絕倫類，詔付史官。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan reign the prefect Xu Jingxian memorialized that Wenzhen's filial piety was peerless in kind, and an edict handed the matter to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Prefect Xu Jingxian reported his filial piety as without parallel, and the throne ordered the historians to record it.

sentences.zh: 沈季詮，字子平，洪州豫章人。

translations.literal: Shen Jiquan, courtesy name Ziping, was a man of Yuzhang in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiquan, styled Ziping, came from Yuzhang in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝，未嘗與人爭，皆以為怯。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother filially and never quarreled with others; all regarded him as cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: Fatherless from boyhood, he devoted himself to his mother and never quarreled—neighbors mistook his gentleness for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 季詮曰：「吾怯乎？

translations.literal: Jiquan said: "Am I cowardly?
translations.idiomatic: Jiquan asked, "Do you call this cowardice?

sentences.zh: 為人子者，可遺憂於親乎哉！」

translations.literal: As one who is someone's child, can one leave worry upon one's parent!
translations.idiomatic: What son would heap trouble on the mother who bore him!

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，侍母度江，遇暴風，母溺死，季詮號呼投江中，少選，持母臂浮出水上。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan reign, while attending his mother in crossing the river, they met a violent wind; his mother drowned and died. Jiquan cried out and cast himself into the river; in a little while he emerged holding his mother's arm above the water.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, escorting his mother across the Yangzi, they were caught in a squall and she drowned. Shen wailed and threw himself in after her; moments later he surfaced, bearing her arm above the flood.

sentences.zh: 都督謝叔方具禮祭而葬之。

translations.literal: The regional inspector Xie Shufang provided full rites, sacrificed, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Xie Shufang conducted the full funeral rites and laid them both to rest.

sentences.zh: 許伯會，越州蕭山人。

translations.literal: Xu Bohui was a man of Xiaoshan in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bohui came from Xiaoshan in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或曰玄度十二世孫。

translations.literal: Some say he was the twelfth-generation descendant of Xuandu.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held him a twelfth-generation descendant of the filial exemplar Xuandu.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉。

translations.literal: He was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the Filial and Incorrupt recommendation.

sentences.zh: 上元中，為衡陽博士。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan reign he served as Erudite of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Shangyuan he was erudite at Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 母喪，負土成墳，不禦絮帛、嘗滋味。

translations.literal: In his mother's mourning he carried earth to form the mound, and would not wear padded silks or taste flavored food.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he piled the grave with his own hands, shunning padded garments and any food with flavor.

sentences.zh: 野火將逮塋樹，悲號於天，俄而雨，火滅。

translations.literal: A wildfire was about to reach the trees of the graveyard; he cried out in grief to Heaven, and in a little while rain fell and the fire was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When wildfire threatened the trees around her tomb, he wailed to Heaven—and rain fell at once, and the flames died.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，泉湧廬前，靈芝生。

translations.literal: In a year of drought a spring gushed forth before his hut, and spirit fungus grew.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year a spring welled up before his mourning hut, and sacred fungus sprang from the ground.

sentences.zh: 陳集原，瀧州開陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Jiyuan was a man of Kaiyang in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiyuan came from Kaiyang in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世為酋長。

translations.literal: For generations his family were chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had led as chieftains for generations.

sentences.zh: 父龍樹，為欽州刺史，有疾，即集原輒不食。

translations.literal: His father Longshu served as Qinzhou prefect; whenever he fell ill, Jiyuan at once would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Longshu was prefect of Qinzhou; whenever Longshu fell ill, Jiyuan would immediately stop eating.

sentences.zh: 及亡，嘔血數升，即塋作廬，盡以田貲讓兄弟，裏人高之。

translations.literal: When he died, Jiyuan vomited several sheng of blood; at once by the grave mound he built a mourning hut, entirely yielding fields and goods to his brothers, and the villagers esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death Jiyuan vomited blood by the quart; he built a hut at the tomb, gave all his land and property to his brothers, and his neighbors held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 武後時，歷右豹韜衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, he successively served as General of the Right Leopard-Tarsus Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose to General of the Right Leopard-Tarsus Guard.

sentences.zh: 陸南金，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Nanjin was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nanjin came from Wu district in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖士季，從同郡顧野王學《左氏春秋》、《司馬史》、《班氏漢書》。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shiji studied the "Zuoshi Chunqiu," the "Sima shi," and the "Banshi Han shu" with Gu Yewang of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shiji had studied the Zuoshi Chunqiu, the Sima shi, and the Banshi Han shu under Gu Yewang, a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為越王侗記室兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In Sui service he was secretary and concurrent tutor-reader to the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as secretarial aide and reader-in-waiting to Yang Tong, Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 侗稱制，擢著作郎。

translations.literal: When Tong assumed the regency, Shiji was promoted to Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong took up the regency, Shiji was promoted to Master of Writings.

sentences.zh: 時王世充將篡逆，侗謂士季曰：「隋有天下三十年，朝果無忠臣乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shichong was about to usurp; Tong said to Shiji: "The Sui have held the empire thirty years—can the court truly lack loyal ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was then on the verge of usurpation. Tong said to Shiji, "The Sui have ruled for thirty years—are there really no loyal ministers left in court?

sentences.zh: 士季對曰：「見危授命，臣宿誌也。

translations.literal: Shiji replied: "To face peril and offer one's life—that is my longstanding resolve as a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji answered, "To meet danger and give up one's life is what I have long resolved to do as your servant.

sentences.zh: 請因啟事為陛下殺之。」

translations.literal: Please let me use an incoming memorial as the occasion to kill him for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Let me seize the next memorial audience and kill him on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 謀泄，停侍讀，乃不克。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; his tutoring post was suspended, and the scheme did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed; his post as tutor was revoked, and the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，終太學博士兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan he ended his career as Doctor of the Grand Academy and concurrent Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he died in office as Doctor of the Grand Academy and Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 南金仕為太常奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Nanjin served as Ritual Officer of the Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin held the post of Ritual Officer in the Directorate of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 開元初，少卿廬崇道抵罪徙嶺南，逃還東都。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, Vice Minister Lu Chongdao was convicted and exiled to Lingnan, then fled back to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Vice Minister Lu Chongdao was sentenced and banished to Lingnan, but escaped and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 南金居母喪，崇道偽稱吊客，入而道其情，南金匿之。

translations.literal: Nanjin was in mourning for his mother; Chongdao falsely claimed to be a mourner paying condolences, entered and told him his plight, and Nanjin hid him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin was observing mourning for his mother. Chongdao came disguised as a condolence visitor, told him his story once inside, and Nanjin concealed him.

sentences.zh: 俄為仇人跡告，詔侍御史王旭捕按，南金當重法，弟趙璧詣旭自言：「匿崇道者我也，請死。」

translations.literal: Soon an enemy traced and reported him; an edict ordered the Attending Censor Wang Xu to arrest and investigate; Nanjin faced severe punishment; his younger brother Zhao Bi went to Xu and declared of himself: "I am the one who hid Chongdao—I ask for death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a foe tracked him down and denounced him to the throne. The emperor ordered Attending Censor Wang Xu to seize and try the case. Nanjin faced a capital sentence. His younger brother Zhao Bi went to Xu and said, "I hid Chongdao. Put me to death.

sentences.zh: 南金固言弟自誣不情，旭怪之，趙璧曰：「母未葬，妹未歸，兄能辦之，我生無益，不如死。」

translations.literal: Nanjin firmly said his brother falsely incriminated himself without truth; Xu marveled at it; Zhao Bi said: "Mother is not yet buried, sister is not yet married—my elder brother can attend to these; my life is of no use; better to die.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin insisted his brother was falsely confessing out of fraternal feeling. Xu was astonished. Zhao Bi said, "Our mother is still unburied and our sister still unwed. My brother can see to both. I am of no further use alive—death is better.

sentences.zh: 旭驚，上狀。

translations.literal: Xu was startled and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Stunned, Xu memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗皆宥之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 南金知書史，履操謹完。

translations.literal: Nanjin was versed in histories, and his conduct in office was careful and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin was learned in history and meticulous in his personal conduct.

sentences.zh: 張說、陸象先以賢謂之，由庫部員外以痼疾改太子洗馬，卒。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue and Lu Xiangxian spoke of him as worthy; from Vice Director in the Treasury Department he was moved to Crown Prince Libationer on account of chronic illness, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue and Lu Xiangxian praised his worth. He rose from Vice Director in the Treasury to Crown Prince Libationer, but chronic illness forced the transfer, and he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 張琇，河中解人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu was a native of Jie in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu came from Jie district in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 父審素，為巂州都督，有陳纂仁者，誣其冒戰級、私庸兵。

translations.literal: His father Shensu was Xi prefect; there was Chen Zanren, who falsely accused him of fraudulently claiming battle merit grades and privately employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shensu served as prefect of Xi. Chen Zanren falsely accused him of inflating battle honors and keeping soldiers for private use.

sentences.zh: 玄宗疑之，詔監察御史楊汪即按。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was suspicious and ordered the Investigating Censor Yang Wang to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and ordered Investigating Censor Yang Wang to look into the case at once.

sentences.zh: 纂仁復告審素與總管董堂禮謀反。

translations.literal: Zanren again reported that Shensu and the commander Dong Tangli were plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zanren then charged that Shensu and the regional commander Dong Tangli were plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是汪收審素系雅州獄，馳至巂州按反狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang arrested Shensu and imprisoned him in Yazhou jail, then galloped to Xi to investigate the rebellion charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang arrested Shensu, threw him into the Yazhou jail, and raced to Xi to verify the treason accusation.

sentences.zh: 堂禮不勝忿，殺纂仁，以兵七百圍汪，脅使露章雪審素罪。

translations.literal: Tangli, unable to bear his rage, killed Zanren, and with seven hundred troops surrounded Wang, coercing him to file an open memorial clearing Shensu's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Tangli, beside himself with fury, killed Zanren, then surrounded Wang with seven hundred men and forced him to submit a public memorial clearing Shensu.

sentences.zh: 既而吏共斬堂禮，汪得出，遂當審素實反，斬之，沒其家。

translations.literal: Before long the clerks together beheaded Tangli; Wang was able to get out; he then judged Shensu guilty of real rebellion, executed him, and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the clerks joined in beheading Tangli, and Wang escaped. He then found Shensu guilty of actual rebellion, executed him, and seized his property.

sentences.zh: 琇與兄皇尚幼，徙嶺南。

translations.literal: Xiu and his elder brother Huang were still young and were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and his elder brother Huang were still boys when the family was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 久之，逃還。

translations.literal: After a long time they fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Years later they slipped back home.

sentences.zh: 汪更名萬頃。

translations.literal: Wang changed his name to Wanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang had taken the new name Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 皇時年十三，琇少二歲。

translations.literal: Huang was then thirteen; Xiu was two years younger.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was thirteen; Xiu two years younger.

sentences.zh: 夜狙萬頃於魏王池，皇斫其馬，萬頃驚，不及鬥，為琇所殺。

translations.literal: By night they ambushed Wanqing at the Pool of the Prince of Wei; Huang hacked his horse; Wanqing was startled and had no time to fight; Xiu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: One night they lay in wait for Wanqing at the Prince of Wei's pool. Huang struck down his horse. Wanqing panicked and never got to fight back before Xiu killed him.

sentences.zh: 條所以殺萬頃狀系於斧，奔江南，將殺構父罪者，然後詣有司。

translations.literal: He itemized the grounds for killing Wanqing and tied the statement to the axe; he fled to the south of the Yangtze, intending to kill those who had framed his father's crime, and only then go to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu wrote out the reasons for the killing and fastened the note to the axe, then fled south of the Yangtze to slay those who had framed his father before surrendering to the law.

sentences.zh: 道汜水，吏捕以聞。

translations.literal: Passing Sishui, an officer arrested them and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui an official seized them and reported to the capital.

sentences.zh: 中書令張九齡等皆稱其孝烈，宜貸死，侍中裴耀卿等陳不可，帝亦謂然，謂九齡曰：「孝子者，義不顧命。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling and others all praised their filial fierceness and said death should be commuted; Vice Minister Pei Yaoging and others argued it could not be done; the Emperor also thought so, and said to Jiuling: "A filial son, in righteousness, does not spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling and others urged that their filial valor warranted sparing their lives. Vice Minister Pei Yaoging and others argued against it. The emperor agreed with Pei and told Jiuling, "A true filial son will not flinch from death for righteousness's sake.

sentences.zh: 殺之可成其誌，赦之則虧律。

translations.literal: To execute them can fulfill their resolve; to pardon them would damage the law.
translations.idiomatic: Execution would complete their purpose; pardon would breach the law.

sentences.zh: 凡為子，孰不願孝？

translations.literal: Who among sons does not wish to be filial?
translations.idiomatic: What son does not long to be filial?

sentences.zh: 轉相仇殺，遂無已時。」

translations.literal: Turn and mutually avenge in killing, and there will be no end.
translations.idiomatic: If each took revenge in turn, killing would never cease.

sentences.zh: 卒用耀卿議，議者以為冤。

translations.literal: In the end he adopted Yaoging's view; commentators held it a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He finally followed Pei Yaoging's counsel, though many thought the brothers were wronged.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔申諭，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict explaining the reasoning, then executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict setting out his reasoning, then had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 臨刑賜食，皇不能進，琇色自如，曰：「下見先人，復何恨！」

translations.literal: At the execution food was granted; Huang could not eat; Xiu's countenance was as calm as ever, and he said: "Going below to meet our forebears—what regret remains!
translations.idiomatic: On the scaffold they were given a last meal. Huang could not swallow; Xiu's face stayed composed. He said, "Soon I shall meet our ancestors below—what is left to regret!

sentences.zh: 人莫不閔之，為誄揭於道，斂錢為葬北邙，尚恐仇人發之，作疑冢，使不知其處。

translations.literal: None did not pity them; they wrote elegies and posted them along the road, collected money to bury them on Beimang; still fearing enemies would disinter them, they made decoy tombs so that no one would know the true site.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw it grieved for them. Elegies were posted along the roads, and money was collected to bury them on Beimang. Fearing the enemy clan might desecrate the graves, they also raised false tombs so the true resting place could not be found.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，有即墨人王君操，父隋末為鄉人李君則所殺，亡命去，時君操尚幼。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizong there was Wang Juncao of Jimo; his father at the end of Sui was killed by a fellow villager, Li Junze, who fled; at the time Juncao was still young.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong there lived Wang Juncao of Jimo. At the close of the Sui his father was murdered by a neighbor, Li Junze, who then fled. Juncao was still a child.

sentences.zh: 至貞觀時，朝世更易，而君操窶孤，仇家無所憚，詣州自言。

translations.literal: By the Zhenguan era the court and age had changed; yet Juncao was poor and isolated; the enemy household had nothing to fear, and Juncao went to the prefecture to declare himself.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhenguan the dynasty had turned over anew. Juncao was destitute and alone, and his enemy no longer feared him—so he went to the prefecture to report the case himself.

sentences.zh: 君操密挾刃殺之，剔其心肝啖立盡，趨告刺史曰：「父死兇手，歷二十年不克報，乃今刷憤，願歸死有司。」

translations.literal: Juncao secretly carried a blade, killed him, gouged out his heart and liver and ate them standing until they were gone, then hurried to tell the prefect: "My father died at a murderer's hand; for twenty years I could not avenge him; only now have I vented my rage—I wish to return and die before the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Juncao had hidden a knife, struck him down, cut out his heart and liver, and devoured them on the spot. He then ran to the prefect and said, "My father was slain by this man. Twenty years I could not settle the score. Today I have at last drained my wrath. I surrender myself to die by the law.

sentences.zh: 州上狀，帝為貸死。

translations.literal: The prefect reported upward; the Emperor commuted the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect memorialized the throne, and the emperor spared his life.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，絳州人趙師舉父為人殺，師舉幼，母改嫁，仇家不疑。

translations.literal: In the time of Gaozong there was Zhao Shiju of Jiangzhou; his father was killed by someone; Shiju was young; his mother remarried; the enemy household did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Zhao Shiju of Jiangzhou lost his father to murder while still a boy. His mother remarried, and the killer's family never suspected him.

sentences.zh: 師舉長，為人庸，夜讀書。

translations.literal: When Shiju grew up he was hired out as a laborer and studied books by night.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he hired himself out by day and read books by night.

sentences.zh: 久之，手殺仇人，詣官自陳，帝原之。

translations.literal: After a long time he personally killed the enemy, went to the office and confessed himself; the Emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In time he killed the murderer with his own hand, walked into the magistrate's office, and confessed. The emperor granted him pardon.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，同官人同蹄智壽父為族人所害，智壽與弟智爽候諸塗，擊殺之，相率歸有司爭為首，有司不能決者三年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, a man of Tongguan, Tong Ti Zhishou—his father had been harmed by clansmen; Zhishou and his younger brother Zhishuang waited along the road and struck them dead, then together went to the authorities each contending to be named chief culprit; for three years the officials could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign, Tong Ti Zhishou of Tongguan learned that clansmen had murdered his father. He and his brother Zhishuang ambushed them on the road and killed them, then marched together to the magistrate's office, each insisting he had led the attack. For three years the court could not settle who was chief culprit.

sentences.zh: 或言弟始謀，乃論死，臨刑曰：「仇已報，死不恨。」

translations.literal: Someone said the younger brother had first plotted it; he was therefore sentenced to death. At the execution he said: "The feud is already avenged; I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the judges that the younger brother had hatched the plot, and he alone was condemned to die. On the scaffold he said, "The score is settled—I have no regret in dying."

sentences.zh: 智壽自投地委頓，身無完膚，舐智爽血盡乃已，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Zhishou threw himself to the ground in collapse; his body had no intact skin; he licked Zhishuang's blood until none remained and then stopped; those who saw it were pained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishou flung himself down in a swoon, his flesh torn everywhere, and licked his brother's blood until none was left. All who witnessed it wept.

sentences.zh: 武後時，下邽人徐元慶父爽為縣尉趙師韞所殺，元慶變姓名為驛家保。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, Xu Yuanqing of Xiayi—his father Shuang had been killed by the county lieutenant Zhao Shiyun; Yuanqing changed his name and became a groom at a relay station.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Xu Yuanqing of Xiayi saw his father Shuang murdered by the county lieutenant Zhao Shiyun. He assumed a false name and hired on as a groom at a post station.

sentences.zh: 久之，師韞以御史舍亭下，元慶手殺之，自囚詣官。

translations.literal: After a long while Shiyun, as censor, lodged at a post pavilion; Yuanqing killed him with his own hand, then bound himself and went to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Shiyun, now a censor, put up at a relay inn. Yuanqing stabbed him to death, then walked in chains to surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 後欲赦死，左拾遺陳子昂議曰：

translations.literal: Later, when they wished to pardon him from death, Left Remonstrator Chen Zi'ang memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the throne later moved to spare him from execution, Left Remonstrator Chen Zi'ang submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 先王立禮以進人，明罰以齊政。

translations.literal: The ancient kings established ritual to advance men and made punishments clear to harmonize governance.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings set up ritual to lift men up and made penalties plain to bring government into order.

sentences.zh: 枕幹仇敵，人子義也；

translations.literal: To sleep with one's shield upon one's father's enemy is a son's duty;
translations.idiomatic: To keep vigil with weapon ready against a father's killer is what a son owes;

sentences.zh: 誅罪禁亂，王政綱也。

translations.literal: to condemn guilt and forbid disorder is the royal government's guiding cord.
translations.idiomatic: to punish crime and bar chaos is the sovereign cord of rule.

sentences.zh: 然無義不可訓人，亂綱不可明法。

translations.literal: Yet without righteousness one cannot instruct the people; with the guiding cord in disorder one cannot clarify the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where righteousness fails, the people cannot be taught; where that cord is tangled, the law cannot be made clear.

sentences.zh: 聖人修禮治內，飭法防外，使守法者不以禮廢刑，居禮者不以法傷義，然後暴亂銷，廉恥興，天下所以直道而行也。

translations.literal: The sage repairs ritual to govern within and disciplines law to guard against without, so that those who keep the law do not set aside punishment for ritual's sake, and those who dwell in ritual do not harm righteousness for law's sake—then violence and disorder are extinguished, integrity and shame arise, and all under Heaven may walk the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: The sage cultivates ritual inward and sharpens law outward, so that law-abiders do not void punishment in the name of ritual, and ritual-abiders do not wound righteousness in the name of law—only then do outrage and rebellion fade, honor and shame revive, and the realm walk the upright road.

sentences.zh: 元慶報父仇，束身歸罪，雖古烈士何以加？

translations.literal: Yuanqing avenged his father's feud, bound himself and surrendered to judgment—what ancient martyr could surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing settled his father's blood-debt and came bound to accept sentence—what hero of antiquity could outdo him?

sentences.zh: 然殺人者死，畫一之制也，法不可二，元慶宜伏辜。

translations.literal: Yet "who kills shall die" is the uniform regulation; the law cannot be twofold; Yuanqing ought to submit to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the single statute stands: life for life. The law admits no double standard; Yuanqing should bear the penalty.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「父仇不同天。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "A father's enemy shares not the same sky."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "With a father's foe one cannot live under the same heaven."

sentences.zh: 勸人之教也。

translations.literal: That is teaching that exhorts men.
translations.idiomatic: That is the teaching meant to stir men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 教之不茍，元慶宜赦。

translations.literal: Were the teaching not strict, Yuanqing ought to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: If that teaching were not held inviolate, Yuanqing would deserve pardon.

sentences.zh: 臣聞刑所以生，遏亂也；

translations.literal: I have heard that punishments exist to give life—that is, to check disorder;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that penalties exist to preserve life—that is, to hold back chaos;

sentences.zh: 仁所以利，崇德也。

translations.literal: humaneness exists to profit—that is, to exalt virtue.
translations.idiomatic: benevolence exists to do good—that is, to raise up virtue.

sentences.zh: 今報父之仇，非亂也；

translations.literal: Now to avenge one's father is not disorder;
translations.idiomatic: To avenge a father today is not chaos;

sentences.zh: 行子之道，仁也。

translations.literal: to walk the son's path is humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: to walk the son's road is benevolence.

sentences.zh: 仁而無利，與同亂誅，是曰能刑，未可以訓。

translations.literal: Humaneness without profit, condemned like common disorder—this may be called the ability to punish, but it cannot instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence that brings no benefit, punished like ordinary riot—one may call that skill in sentencing, but it cannot teach the people.

sentences.zh: 然則邪由正生，治必亂作，故禮防不勝，先王以制刑也。

translations.literal: For then wickedness is born from the right, and order necessarily breeds disorder; ritual's defenses do not prevail, and therefore the ancient kings established punishments.
translations.idiomatic: For evil springs from what is upright, and order itself breeds turmoil when ritual's bulwarks fail—hence the former kings forged penal law.

sentences.zh: 今義元慶之節，則廢刑也。

translations.literal: Now to justify Yuanqing's conduct is to abolish punishment.
translations.idiomatic: To honor Yuanqing's act of righteousness now is to cast punishment aside.

sentences.zh: 跡元慶所以能義動天下，以其忘生而及於德也。

translations.literal: Trace why Yuanqing could move the world by righteousness—it is that he forgot life and attained virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how he moved the realm by righteousness: he forgot his life and reached virtue.

sentences.zh: 若釋罪以利其生，是奪其德，虧其義，非所謂殺身成仁、全死忘生之節。

translations.literal: If one released guilt to profit his life, that would seize his virtue and diminish his righteousness; it would not be what is called the conduct of dying to achieve humanity and wholly forgetting life in facing death.
translations.idiomatic: To absolve him for the sake of keeping him alive would strip away his virtue and wound his righteousness—it would not be the stature of one who dies to perfect humanity and meets death forgetful of life.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜正國之典，寘之以刑，然後旌閭墓可也。

translations.literal: I hold that one ought first to uphold the state's canonical law and place him under punishment; only then may gate and tomb be commended.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the national code should first be upheld and he subjected to sentence; only afterward may his lane and grave be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 時韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time all approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The court at the time endorsed his view.

sentences.zh: 後禮部員外郎柳宗元駁曰：

translations.literal: Later Ministerial Aide in the Ministry of Rites Liu Zongyuan rebutted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Zongyuan, Ministerial Aide in the Ministry of Rites, wrote in rebuttal:

sentences.zh: 禮之大本，以防亂也。

translations.literal: The root of ritual is likewise to guard against disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The great root of ritual, too, is to ward off chaos.

sentences.zh: 若曰：無為賊虐，凡為子者殺無赦。

translations.literal: It may be said: Do not act as brigand and tyrant; any who is a son—slay without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: One may put it thus: commit no robbery or cruelty—whoever is a son, put to death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 刑之大本，亦以防亂也。

translations.literal: The root of punishment is also to guard against disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The great root of penal law is likewise to ward off chaos.

sentences.zh: 若曰：無為賊虐，凡為治者殺無赦。

translations.literal: It may be said: Do not act as brigand and tyrant; any who governs—slay without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: One may put it thus: commit no robbery or cruelty—whoever holds office, put to death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 其本則合，其用則異。

translations.literal: Their roots agree; their applications differ.
translations.idiomatic: Their foundations are one; their uses diverge.

sentences.zh: 旌與誅，不得並也。

translations.literal: Commendation and execution cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: Public honor and capital punishment cannot be joined.

sentences.zh: 誅其可旌，茲謂濫，黷刑甚矣；

translations.literal: To execute one who may be commended—this is called excess; how extreme the abuse of punishment!
translations.idiomatic: To execute a man fit for praise is excess—an abuse of sentencing past bearing;

sentences.zh: 旌其可誅，茲謂僭，壞禮甚矣。

translations.literal: To commend one who ought to be executed—this is called overstepping; how extreme the injury to ritual!
translations.idiomatic: to praise a man fit for execution is presumption—a wound to ritual past bearing.

sentences.zh: 若師韞獨以私怨，奮吏氣，虐非辜，州牧不知罪，刑官不知問，上下蒙冒，籲號不聞。

translations.literal: If Shiyun alone, out of private animus, flared the arrogance of an official, tormented the innocent, and neither the prefect knew guilt nor the sentencing official knew to inquire—superiors and inferiors shrouded in deceit, cries of anguish unheard—
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Shiyun alone, nursing private spite, let an officer's swagger run wild and tortured the guiltless, while the prefect never charged a crime and the judge never held an inquiry—high and low wrapped in concealment, wails of the wronged never reaching the throne—

sentences.zh: 而元慶能處心積慮以沖仇人之胸，介然自克，即死無憾，是守禮而行義也。

translations.literal: yet Yuanqing could lodge in his heart and accumulate resolve until he pierced the enemy's breast, by himself restrained and resolute, and at death without regret—this is keeping ritual and practicing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: yet Yuanqing could brood and plan until he drove the blade into his foe's breast, upright and self-mastered, content even in death—that is to keep ritual and walk in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 執事者宜有慚色，將謝之不暇，而又何誅焉？

translations.literal: Those in office ought to show shame; they would have no leisure for thanks, so how execute him?
translations.idiomatic: Men in office ought to blush; they would scarcely have breath to apologize—how then put him to death?

sentences.zh: 其或父不免於罪，師韞之誅，不愆於法，是非死於吏也，是死於法也。

translations.literal: But if perhaps the father could not escape guilt, and Shiyun's execution was not in violation of law—that was not dying at an official's hands but dying at the law's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the father could not escape conviction, and Shiyun's punishment broke no statute—that was death by law, not death at an officer's whim.

sentences.zh: 法其可仇乎？

translations.literal: Can the law be made an enemy?
