translations.idiomatic: Can one treat the law itself as a foe?

sentences.zh: 仇天子之法，而戕奉法之吏，是悖驁而淩上也。

translations.literal: To treat the Son of Heaven's law as an enemy and slay an officer who bears the law—that is rebellion and arrogance, trespass against superiors.
translations.idiomatic: To hate the Son of Heaven's law and cut down the officer who carries it out is defiance and insolence, an assault upon authority.

sentences.zh: 執而誅之，所以正邦典，而又何旌焉？

translations.literal: To seize and execute him is how to rectify the state's canonical law—so how commend him?
translations.idiomatic: To arrest and execute him is to set the national code straight—so where is room for praise?

sentences.zh: 禮之所謂仇者，冤抑沈痛而號無告也，非謂抵罪觸法，陷於大戮，而曰彼殺之我乃殺之，不議曲直，暴寡脅弱而已。

translations.literal: What ritual calls "enemy" is one wronged, submerged in pain, who cries with no one to hear—not one who incurred guilt and touched the law, fell into great execution, and then said "he killed so I kill," without debating right and wrong, merely bullying the few and coercing the weak.
translations.idiomatic: The foe ritual speaks of is one crushed by injustice, drowning in grief, whose cry finds no ear—not one who broke the law, faced the supreme penalty, and then said, "He killed, so I kill," without weighing right from wrong, merely preying on the helpless.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「父不受誅，子復仇可也；

translations.literal: The "Zuo Commentary" says: "If the father was not punished, the son may take revenge;
translations.idiomatic: The "Zuo Commentary" says, "If the father was not condemned, the son may avenge him;

sentences.zh: 父受誅，子復仇，此推刃之道。

translations.literal: if the father was punished, the son takes revenge—this is the way of passing the blade along.
translations.idiomatic: if the father was condemned and the son still avenges him, that is the road of passing the blade onward.

sentences.zh: 復仇不除害。」

translations.literal: Revenge does not remove the harm."
translations.idiomatic: Vengeance does not clear the wrong."

sentences.zh: 今若取此以斷兩下相殺，則合於禮矣。

translations.literal: Now if one takes this to judge mutual killing between inferior and superior, it accords with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Apply that rule to a killing between high and low, and the case falls within ritual.

sentences.zh: 且夫不忘仇，孝也；

translations.literal: Moreover, not forgetting one's feud is filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Not to forget the feud is filial;

sentences.zh: 不愛死，義也。

translations.literal: not cherishing one's life is righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: not to cling to life is righteous.

sentences.zh: 元慶能不越於禮，服孝死義，是必達理而聞道者也。

translations.literal: Yuan Qing was able not to overstep ritual; he served filial piety and died for righteousness—he must be one who comprehended principle and heard the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qing never stepped outside ritual bounds: he lived filial piety and died for righteousness. Surely he was a man who had grasped principle and truly heard the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫達理聞道之人，豈其以王法為敵仇者哉！

translations.literal: As for one who comprehends principle and hears the Way—how could he take the king's law as an enemy foe!
translations.idiomatic: A man who comprehends principle and hears the Way—would he ever treat the king's law as his enemy?

sentences.zh: 議者反以為戮，黷刑壞禮，其不可以為典明矣。

translations.literal: Yet the deliberators instead treated him as fit for execution—abusive punishment that wrecks ritual; this plainly cannot serve as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court turned around and marked him for execution—an abusive sentence that shatters ritual. That plainly cannot stand as precedent.

sentences.zh: 請下臣議附於令，有斷斯獄者，不宜以前議從事。

translations.literal: I request that the ministers' deliberations be appended to the statutes; whoever tries this kind of case ought not follow the prior deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that our deliberation be entered into the statutes, so that anyone who judges such a case hereafter will not be bound by the earlier opinion.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，衢州人余常安父、叔皆為裏人謝全所殺。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xianzong, Yu Chang'an of Quzhou—both his father and uncle—were killed by a fellow townsman, Xie Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong, Yu Chang'an of Quzhou saw both his father and uncle killed by a neighbor, Xie Quan.

sentences.zh: 常安八歲，已能謀復仇。

translations.literal: Chang'an was eight and already plotting revenge.
translations.idiomatic: At eight years old Chang'an was already plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 十有七年，卒殺全。

translations.literal: Seventeen years later he finally killed Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years on, he at last killed Quan.

sentences.zh: 刺史元錫奏輕比，刑部尚書李鄘執不可，卒抵死。

translations.literal: Prefect Yuan Xi memorialized for a lighter sentence; Minister of Justice Li Yong insisted it could not be done; in the end he died by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yuan Xi urged a lighter sentence, but Minister of Justice Li Yong would not yield, and in the end Chang'an was executed.

sentences.zh: 又富平人梁悅父為秦果所殺，悅殺仇，詣縣請罪。

translations.literal: Also: Liang Yue of Fuping—his father was killed by Qin Guo; Yue killed the foe and went to the county to confess his crime.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liang Yue of Fuping, whose father had been killed by Qin Guo. Yue slew his enemy and went to the county magistrate to surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「在《禮》父仇不同天，而法殺人必死。

translations.literal: An edict said: "As the "Book of Rites" states, a father's enmity cannot share the same heaven with you, yet in law, killing a person must mean death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "As the "Book of Rites" states, a father's enemy cannot share the same heaven with his son, yet the law demands death for anyone who kills.

sentences.zh: 禮、法，王教大端也，二說異焉。

translations.literal: Ritual and law are the great foundations of royal instruction—yet the two doctrines diverge here.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and law are the twin pillars of royal teaching, yet here the two teachings pull apart.

sentences.zh: 下尚書省議。」

translations.literal: Refer it down to the Secretariat for deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter be referred to the Secretariat for deliberation."

sentences.zh: 職方員外郎韓愈曰：

translations.literal: Vice Director of Personnel Han Yu said:
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Personnel Han Yu submitted:

sentences.zh: 子復父仇，見於《春秋》、於《禮記》、《周官》，若子史，不勝數，未有非而罪者。

translations.literal: A son avenging his father's foe appears in the "Spring and Autumn Annals," in the "Record of Rites," in the "Rites of Zhou," and in histories if sons were listed—they cannot be counted; never has one been deemed wrong and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Sons who avenged their fathers appear in the "Spring and Autumn Annals," the "Record of Rites," and the "Rites of Zhou," and in histories beyond number—never once were they judged wrong and punished.

sentences.zh: 最宜詳於律，而律無條，非闕文也。

translations.literal: This matter ought above all to be spelled out in the statutes, yet the statutes have no article—this is not a lacuna in the text.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what statutes ought to spell out, yet the code contains no article on it—not because the text is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 蓋以為不許復仇，則傷孝子之心；

translations.literal: Presumably because to forbid revenge would wound the filial son's heart;
translations.idiomatic: The reason, I believe, is that forbidding revenge would break a filial son's heart;

sentences.zh: 許復仇，則人將倚法顓殺，無以禁止。

translations.literal: to permit revenge, and people will lean on the law to kill wantonly, with no way to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: yet permitting it would let men lean on the law to kill at will, with no way to stop them.

sentences.zh: 夫律雖本於聖人，然執而行之者，有司也。

translations.literal: Statutes may derive from the sages, yet those who grasp and enforce them are the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Though statutes spring from the sages, it is officials who grasp and apply them.

sentences.zh: 經之所明者，制有司者也。

translations.literal: What the classics illuminate is what restrains the officials.
translations.idiomatic: What the classics make clear is what binds those officials.

sentences.zh: 丁寧其義於經而深沒其文於律者，將使法吏一斷於法，而經術之士得引經以議也。

translations.literal: To set the meaning clearly in the classics while burying the wording deep in the statutes is meant to let law officers decide solely by statute, while scholars of the classics may cite the classics in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: To lodge the meaning plainly in the classics while burying the letter deep in the statutes is to let law officers judge by statute alone, while men versed in the classics may still bring the classics to bear in debate.

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰：「凡殺人而義者，令勿仇，仇之則死。」

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" says: "Whenever one kills a person righteously, order that he not be avenged; if avenged, then death.'
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" states: "When anyone kills with justification, command that he not be avenged; if he is avenged, the avenger dies.'

sentences.zh: 義者，宜也。

translations.literal: Righteous' means 'fitting.'"
translations.idiomatic: Righteous' means fitting."

sentences.zh: 明殺人而不得其宜者，子得復仇也。

translations.literal: Clearly when one kills without its being fitting, the son may avenge.
translations.idiomatic: Where the killing was plainly unfitting, the son may take revenge.

sentences.zh: 此百姓之相仇者也。

translations.literal: This is the mutual enmity among common people.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns private blood-feuds among commoners.

sentences.zh: 公羊子曰：「父不受誅，子復仇可也。」

translations.literal: Gongyangzi said: "If the father did not receive lawful punishment, the son may avenge—this is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Gongyangzi says: "If the father was not lawfully executed, the son may avenge him."

sentences.zh: 不受誅者，罪不當誅也。

translations.literal: 'Did not receive lawful punishment' means the crime did not warrant execution.
translations.idiomatic: 'Did not receive lawful punishment' means the offense did not merit death.

sentences.zh: 誅者，上施下之辭，非百姓相殺也。

translations.literal: " 'Punishment' is the terminology of the superior applying to the inferior—not common people killing one another.
translations.idiomatic: " 'Execution' is the language of the ruler imposing sentence from above—not of commoners killing one another.

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰：「凡報仇讎者，書於士，殺之無罪。」

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" says: "Whoever is to avenge enmity shall register it with the official; if he kills, there is no crime."
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" also says: "Whoever intends to avenge a wrong shall record it with the magistrate; if he then kills, he is without guilt."

sentences.zh: 言將復仇，必先言於官，則無罪也。

translations.literal: This means that intending revenge, one must first speak to the authorities—then there is no crime.
translations.idiomatic: That is to say: before taking revenge, one must first declare it to the authorities—only then is there no crime.

sentences.zh: 復仇之名雖同，而其事各異。

translations.literal: The name "revenge" may be the same, yet the circumstances differ.
translations.idiomatic: The word revenge is one, but the cases are not the same.

sentences.zh: 或百姓相仇，如《周官》所稱，可議於今者；

translations.literal: Some are commoners avenging among themselves, as the "Rites of Zhou" describes—these may be deliberated under present policy;
translations.idiomatic: Some are feuds among commoners, as the "Rites of Zhou" describes—these may still be weighed under present law;

sentences.zh: 或為官吏所誅，如《公羊》所稱，不可行於今者。

translations.literal: some concern execution by officials, as the "Gongyang Commentary" describes—these cannot be practiced today.
translations.idiomatic: some concern fathers put to death by officials, as the "Gongyang Commentary" describes—these cannot be applied today.

sentences.zh: 《周官》所稱：將復仇先告於士，若孤稚羸弱，抱微誌而伺敵人之便，恐不能自言，未可以為斷於今也。

translations.literal: What the "Rites of Zhou" describes—intending revenge, first reporting to the official—if one is orphaned, young, feeble, or weak, harboring a small resolve while waiting for the enemy's opening, fearing one cannot speak for oneself—this cannot yet serve as a rule for judgment today.
translations.idiomatic: As for the "Rites of Zhou" rule that one must report before avenging: an orphan, a child, the feeble or weak, nursing a small resolve while watching for the enemy's moment, unable to speak for himself—this cannot yet be made the sole standard for judgment today.

sentences.zh: 然則殺之與赦不可一，宜定其制曰：「有復父仇者，事發，具其事下尚書省，集議以聞，酌處之。」

translations.literal: Yet execution and pardon cannot be uniform; a rule should be fixed, saying: "Whoever avenges a father's foe—when the matter arises, set forth the facts and refer them down to the Secretariat; assemble deliberation and report upward; dispose as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Execution and pardon cannot be one rule for all. A statute should be fixed, reading: "When anyone avenges a father's murder, upon the matter coming to light, the full facts shall be sent down to the Secretariat; deliberation shall be assembled and reported upward, and disposition made accordingly."

sentences.zh: 則經無失指矣。

translations.literal: Then the classics will not miss their aim.
translations.idiomatic: Then the intent of the classics will not be lost.

sentences.zh: 有詔以悅申冤，請罪詣公門，流循州。

translations.literal: An edict held that Yue had presented his grievance; he had confessed at the public gate and was exiled to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled that because Yue had voiced his grievance and surrendered himself at the capital gate, he was exiled to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆宗世，京兆人康買得，年十四，父憲責錢於雲陽張蒞，蒞醉，拉憲危死。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Muzong, Kang Maide of the capital district, aged fourteen—his father Xian was collecting a debt from Zhang Li of Yunyang; Li was drunk, dragged Xian, and nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Muzong, Kang Maide of the capital district was fourteen. His father Xian had gone to Yunyang to collect a debt from Zhang Li. Li, drunk, seized Xian and dragged him until he was near death.

sentences.zh: 買得以蒞趫悍，度救不足解，則舉鍤擊其首，三日蒞死。

translations.literal: Maide saw that Li was violent and fierce; judging that rescue could not quickly free his father, he raised a spade and struck his head; three days later Li died.
translations.idiomatic: Maide saw that Li was violent and brutal; judging that help could not arrive in time to free his father, he lifted a spade and struck Li's head. Three days later Li died.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎孫革建言：「買得救父難不為暴，度不解而擊不為兇。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Sun Ge submitted: "Maide saved his father from peril—this is not outrage; judging that relief could not come quickly and striking is not murderous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Sun Ge argued: "Maide rescued his father from deadly peril—that is not wanton violence; seeing that rescue could not come in time and striking is not murderous intent.

sentences.zh: 先王制刑，必先父子之親。

translations.literal: The former kings fashioned punishment, putting the bond of father and son first.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings fashioned punishments with the bond between father and son foremost.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》原心定罪，《周書》諸罰有權。

translations.literal: The "Spring and Autumn Annals" assesses the heart in fixing guilt; the "Book of Documents" allows discretion in penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The "Spring and Autumn Annals" judges by the heart in fixing guilt; the "Book of Documents" grants latitude in every penalty.

sentences.zh: 買得孝性天至，宜賜矜宥。」

translations.literal: Maide's filial nature reached heaven's decree; he ought to be granted compassionate pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Maide's filial nature was heaven-sent; he deserves compassionate pardon.

sentences.zh: 有詔減死。

translations.literal: An edict reduced his death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commuted his death sentence.

sentences.zh: 侯知道、程俱羅者，靈州靈武人。

translations.literal: Hou Zhidao and Cheng Juluo were natives of Lingwu in Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhidao and Cheng Juluo were from Lingwu in Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，穿壙作冢，皆身執其勞，鄉人助者，即哭而卻之。

translations.literal: While in mourning for their parents, in digging the grave and building the tumulus they personally undertook every task; when townsfolk offered help, they wept and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for their parents, they dug the grave and raised the mound with their own hands. When neighbors offered help, they wept and turned them away.

sentences.zh: 廬墳次，哭泣無節，知道七年、俱羅三年不止。

translations.literal: They dwelt by the tomb; weeping beyond measure—Zhidao for seven years, Juluo for three, without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They lived beside the graves, weeping without restraint—Zhidao for seven years, Juluo for three, and would not stop.

sentences.zh: 知道垢塵積首，率夜半傅墳，踴而哭，鳥獸為悲號。

translations.literal: Zhidao's head was heaped with dust and grime; he would habitually at midnight press against the mound, leap and wail, and birds and beasts joined in sorrowful cries.
translations.idiomatic: Dust and grime matted Zhidao's hair; night after night he would press against the mound, leap and wail, until birds and beasts cried out in grief beside him.

sentences.zh: 李華作《二孝贊》表其行，曰：「厥初生人，有君有親。

translations.literal: Li Hua wrote "Eulogy to the Two Filial Sons" to set forth their conduct, saying: "At first when humans arose, there were rulers and there were parents.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hua composed the "Eulogy to the Two Filial Sons" to celebrate their conduct, writing: "When humankind first arose, there were rulers and there were parents.

sentences.zh: 孝親為子，忠君為臣。

translations.literal: To honor parents is the son's part; to be loyal to the ruler is the minister's part.
translations.idiomatic: To honor one's parents is the son's duty; to be loyal to one's ruler is the minister's.

sentences.zh: 兆自天命，降及人倫。

translations.literal: The omen comes from Heaven's mandate, descending to human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The sign issues from Heaven's mandate, descending into the order of human bonds.

sentences.zh: 背死不義，忘生不仁。

translations.literal: To turn one's back on the dead is unrighteous; to forget the living is inhumane.
translations.idiomatic: Who forsakes the dead betrays righteousness; who forgets the living abandons humanity.

sentences.zh: 過及智就，為之禮文。

translations.literal: When transgression reaches its limit, wisdom completes it; ritual forms are fashioned for such deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When excess has run its course, wisdom brings it to rest—and ritual gives such deeds their proper shape.

sentences.zh: 至哉侯氏，創巨病殷。

translations.literal: How supreme the Hou clan!—wounds vast, affliction deep.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme indeed, the House of Hou—grief wound-deep, sorrow beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 手足胼胝，以成高墳。

translations.literal: Hands and feet callused and rough, they thereby completed the lofty mound.
translations.idiomatic: Their palms and soles grew thick with toil until the high tomb stood finished.

sentences.zh: 夜黑飈動，如臨鬼神。

translations.literal: When night was black and gales rose, it was as though spirits stood before them.
translations.idiomatic: In the black of night, when wind howled, they seemed to stand before ghosts and gods.

sentences.zh: 哭無常聲，迥徹蒼旻。

translations.literal: Their weeping had no fixed rhythm; it rang through the azure heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Their cries knew no measure, piercing the wide vault of sky.

sentences.zh: 苴斬三年，爾獨終身。

translations.literal: Coarse hemp and the severest mourning last three years—yet you alone mourn for life.
translations.idiomatic: Sackcloth and the deepest cut of mourning end in three years—yet you alone grieve for a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 嗟嗟程生，其哀也均。

translations.literal: Alas, alas, Scholar Cheng—your grief matches his.
translations.idiomatic: Ah, Cheng—your sorrow is his equal.

sentences.zh: 顧後絕配，瞻前無鄰。」

translations.literal: Looking back, no peer can be paired; gazing forward, no neighbor stands beside."
translations.idiomatic: Behind you, none can be matched; before you, none stands as kin."

sentences.zh: 又有何澄粹者，池州人。

translations.literal: There was also He Chengcui, a man of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also He Chengcui, from Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 親病日錮，俗尚鬼，病者不進藥。

translations.literal: His parent's illness worsened daily; custom favored spirit-mediums, and the sick took no medicine.
translations.idiomatic: As his parent's illness tightened day by day, local custom favored shamans, and the sick refused medicine.

sentences.zh: 澄粹剔股肉進，親疾為瘳。

translations.literal: Chengcui carved flesh from his thigh and presented it; his parent's illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Chengcui cut flesh from his thigh and offered it—and his parent's sickness was healed.

sentences.zh: 後親沒，伏於墓，哭踴無數，以毀卒，當時號「青陽孝子」，士為作誄甚眾。

translations.literal: Later, when his parent died, he lay prostrate at the tomb, weeping and leaping beyond count, and died from grief-wrecked health. Of the age they called him "the Filial Son of Qingyang"; scholars composed many dirges for him.
translations.idiomatic: After his parent died, he lay at the grave, weeping and stamping beyond number until grief destroyed him. His age called him "the Filial Son of Qingyang," and gentlemen wrote dirges for him in great profusion.

sentences.zh: 壽州安豐李興亦有至行，柳宗元為作《孝門銘》，曰：「壽州刺史臣承思言：『九月丁亥，安豐令上所部編戶氓興，父被惡疾，歲月就亟，興自刃股肉，假托饋獻，父老病已不能啖，宿而死。

translations.literal: Li Xing of Anfeng in Shouzhou likewise possessed utmost conduct; Liu Zongyuan wrote for him "Inscription on the Gate of Filial Piety," saying: "The prefect of Shouzhou, your servant Cheng Si, reports: 'On the dinghai day of the ninth month, Xing—a commoner of the registered households in the jurisdiction reported by the magistrate of Anfeng—his father suffered a dire malady; as the months advanced it grew urgent. Xing himself sliced flesh from his thigh, claiming it was food offered in tribute. His father's aged illness had already left him unable to eat; after one night he died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing of Anfeng in Shouzhou likewise showed supreme devotion; Liu Zongyuan composed for him the "Inscription on the Gate of Filial Piety," which reads: "The prefect of Shouzhou, your servant Cheng Si, states: 'On the dinghai day of the ninth month, the magistrate of Anfeng presented Xing, a registered-household commoner of the district: his father was stricken with a grievous illness that worsened with the passing months. Xing cut flesh from his own thigh and passed it off as a gift of food. His father, too weak to eat, died the next night.

sentences.zh: 興號呼撫臆，口鼻垂血，捧土就墳，沾漬涕洟。

translations.literal: Xing cried out, clutching his breast; blood dripped from mouth and nose; he gathered earth to raise the mound, soaking it with tears and rheum.
translations.idiomatic: Xing wailed and beat his chest until blood ran from mouth and nose; he cupped earth for the grave, steeping it in tears and mucus.

sentences.zh: 墳左作小廬，蒙以苫茨，伏匿其中，扶服頓踴，晝夜哭訴。

translations.literal: Beside the mound he built a small hut, roofed with thatch; he hid himself within, leaning on the staff of mourning, prostrating and leaping, weeping and lamenting day and night.
translations.idiomatic: To the grave's left he raised a small hut roofed in thatch and hid himself there, staff in hand, bowing and stamping, weeping and pleading through day and night.

sentences.zh: 孝誠幽達，神為見異，廬上產紫芝、白芝，廬中醴泉湧。

translations.literal: His filial sincerity reached the hidden realm; the spirits manifested wonders: purple and white fungus grew atop the hut, and a sweet spring welled up within.
translations.idiomatic: His filial heart pierced the unseen; the spirits showed signs—purple and white sacred fungus on the hut's roof, a sweet spring bubbling inside.

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下孝治神化，陰中其心，而克致斯事。

translations.literal: All this proceeds from Your Majesty's governance through filial piety and divine transformation, striking his heart from the unseen and enabling him to bring such things to pass.
translations.idiomatic: All this springs from Your Majesty's rule by filial piety and divine transformation, moving his heart in secret until such deeds could be achieved.

sentences.zh: 謹按興匹庶賤陋，循習淺下，性非文字所導，生與耨耒為業，而能鐘彼醇孝，超出古烈，天意神道，猶錫瑞物以表殊異。

translations.literal: Respectfully considered: Xing matches commoners—lowly and plain, shallow in custom and habit, his nature not shaped by the written word; all his life he worked the hoe and plough—yet he could concentrate that pure filial piety, surpassing the heroes of old. Heaven's intent and the spirit-way even bestowed auspicious objects to mark his exceptionality.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that Xing is a common man—humble in station, shallow in learning, untrained by books, who lived by hoe and plough—yet he gathered pure filial devotion that outstripped the worthies of antiquity. Heaven and the spirit-way even granted omens to proclaim his singularity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下有唐堯如神之德，宜加旌褒，合於上下。

translations.literal: Humbly: Your Majesty possesses virtue like unto divine Yao of Tang; he ought to receive commendation and reward, in accord above and below.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit that Your Majesty bears the godlike virtue of Tang Yao; such a man should be honored and rewarded, fitting heaven above and earth below.

sentences.zh: 請表其裏閭，刻石明白，宣延風美，觀示後祀，永無極。

translations.literal: I ask that his lane and hamlet be marked, that stone be carved with clear record, that his exemplary grace be spread abroad, displayed for generations to come, without end.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that his neighborhood be marked, stone carved to make it plain, his shining example spread abroad and shown to posterity without limit.

sentences.zh: 臣昧死請。』

translations.literal: Your servant, risking death, petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dares this petition at peril of his life.

sentences.zh: 制曰可。

translations.literal: The decree replied: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply read: Granted.

sentences.zh: 銘曰：『懿厥孝思，茲惟淑靈。

translations.literal: The inscription reads: 'Deep is this filial thought—here is a pure spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription says: 'How deep his filial mind—here is a noble soul.

sentences.zh: 稟承粹和，篤守天經。

translations.literal: He received the pure and harmonious, steadfastly kept heaven's constant.
translations.idiomatic: He took up pure harmony and held fast to heaven's law.

sentences.zh: 泣侍羸疾，默禱隱冥。

translations.literal: Weeping he attended the wasting illness, silently praying in the hidden dark.
translations.idiomatic: In tears he nursed the failing sickness, praying in silence to the hidden powers.

sentences.zh: 引刃自向，殘肌敗形。

translations.literal: He drew the blade against himself, maiming flesh and ruining form.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the blade on his own body, tearing flesh and breaking his frame.

sentences.zh: 羞膳奉進，憂勞孝誠。

translations.literal: He presented the delicacies in offering, grieving with laboring filial sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the fine food in tribute, worn down by anxious filial care.

sentences.zh: 惟時高高，曾不視聽。

translations.literal: Yet the high one above never looked or listened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the father on high would not see or hear.

sentences.zh: 創巨痛仍，號於穹旻。

translations.literal: Wounds vast, pain unending—he cried out to the vaulted sky.
translations.idiomatic: Grief vast, pain unceasing—he called to the arching heavens.

sentences.zh: 捧土濡涕，頓首成墳。

translations.literal: Cupping earth soaked with tears, he beat his brow until the mound was made.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered earth wet with tears, striking his forehead until the tomb rose.

sentences.zh: 搯膺腐眥，寒暑在廬。

translations.literal: He clawed his breast until the corners of his eyes rotted; cold and heat he endured in the hut.
translations.idiomatic: He tore at his chest until his eyes grew raw; through winter cold and summer heat he kept to the hut.

sentences.zh: 草木悴死，鳥獸踟躕。

translations.literal: Plants withered and died; birds and beasts paced in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees withered away; birds and beasts circled in anguish.

sentences.zh: 殊類異族，亦相其哀。

translations.literal: Strange kinds and alien tribes likewise shared in his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Even alien peoples and strange creatures mourned with him.

sentences.zh: 肇有二位，孝道爰興。

translations.literal: From the beginning there were the two stations; filial piety thereby arose.
translations.idiomatic: When the two roles first stood, filial duty was born.

sentences.zh: 克脩厥猷，載籍是登。

translations.literal: He could cultivate that design and ascend into the written record.
translations.idiomatic: He perfected that path and earned his place in the annals.

sentences.zh: 在帝有虞，以孝烝烝。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shun of the Youyu line, filial piety flourished abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Emperor Shun, filial hearts multiplied.

sentences.zh: 仲尼述經，以教於曾。

translations.literal: Confucius set forth the classics to teach Zengzi.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius laid down the canon to instruct Zeng.

sentences.zh: 惟昔魯侯，見命夷宮。

translations.literal: Long ago the Marquis of Lu was summoned at the Yi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the Lord of Lu received his charge in the Yi chamber.

sentences.zh: 亦有考叔，寤莊稱純。

translations.literal: There was also Kaoshu, who in waking told Zhuang and was praised as pure.
translations.idiomatic: There was Kaoshu too, who woke Duke Zhuang and was hailed as wholly filial.

sentences.zh: 顯顯李氏，實與之倫。

translations.literal: Bright and manifest, the Li clan—truly their peer.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant the House of Li—truly of that company.

sentences.zh: 哀嗟道路，涕慕裏鄰。

translations.literal: Roads echoed with sighs of grief; lanes brimmed with tears of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers on the road wept aloud; neighbors within the lanes wept in longing.

sentences.zh: 神錫秘祉，三秀靈泉。

translations.literal: The spirits bestowed secret blessings; thrice-sprouting growth and a numinous spring.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits granted hidden blessings—auspicious growth in triple shoots and a sacred spring.

sentences.zh: 帝命薦加，亦表其門。

translations.literal: The emperor commanded commendation and advancement, and also marked their gate for honor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Son ordered rewards and distinctions, and set a mark of honor upon their gate.

sentences.zh: 統一上下，交贊天人。

translations.literal: Above and below were unified; Heaven and humanity acclaimed one another.
translations.idiomatic: High and low were brought into accord; Heaven and humankind praised each other in turn.

sentences.zh: 建此碑號，億齡揚芬。』」

translations.literal: This stele inscription was raised, its fragrance to spread for endless ages.'"
translations.idiomatic: This monument was raised, its renown to bloom through endless generations.'"

sentences.zh: 許法慎，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: Xu Fashen was a native of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fashen was from Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甫三歲，已有知。

translations.literal: At only three years he already had understanding.
translations.idiomatic: At three he already showed uncommon sense.

sentences.zh: 時母病，不飲乳，慘慘有憂色。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he would not nurse; his face was drawn with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew ill, he refused the breast and wore a face hollow with worry.

sentences.zh: 或以珍餌詭悅之，輒不食，還以進母。

translations.literal: If someone tried to coax him with fine delicacies, he would not eat but brought them back to present to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When others offered rare delicacies to cheer him, he would not touch them but carried them back to his mother.

sentences.zh: 後親喪，常廬於塋，有甘露、嘉禾、靈芝、木連理、白兔之祥。

translations.literal: After his parents' deaths, he constantly kept a mourning hut at the grave; there were omens of sweet dew, fine grain, lingzhi, trees with conjoined trunks, and a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he kept constant vigil in a hut beside the tomb—and sweet dew fell, grain grew fair, lingzhi sprouted, trees joined in a single trunk, and a white rabbit appeared.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，表異其閭。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, his lane was publicly honored for these marvels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign, his neighborhood was publicly honored for these signs.

sentences.zh: 林攢，泉州莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Zan was a native of Putian in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zan was from Putian in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，仕為福唐尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era, he served as aide to the magistrate of Futang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign he held office as aide to the magistrate of Futang.

sentences.zh: 母羸老，未及迎而病。

translations.literal: His mother was frail and aged; before he could go to fetch her, she fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was frail and old; before he could bring her to him, she took ill.

sentences.zh: 攢聞，棄官還。

translations.literal: On hearing this, Zan resigned his post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard, Zan abandoned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 及母亡，水漿不入口五日。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he took neither water nor food for five days.
translations.idiomatic: At her death he took neither water nor food for five days.

sentences.zh: 自埏甓作冢，廬其右，有白烏來，甘露降。

translations.literal: He himself laid bricks and built the tomb, kept a hut to its right; a white crow came and sweet dew fell.
translations.idiomatic: He molded bricks and raised the tomb himself, then kept a mourning hut to its right—a white crow came, and sweet dew descended.

sentences.zh: 觀察使李若初遣官屬驗實，會露晞，裏人失色，攢哭曰：「天所降露，禍我邪？」

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner Li Ruochu sent subordinates to verify the marvels; just as the dew dried in the sun, the villagers turned pale—Zan wept and cried: "The dew Heaven sent—is it sent to bring me harm?"
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Li Ruochu sent officials to verify the signs; the dew happened to dry in the sun, and the villagers blanched. Zan wept aloud: "Has the dew Heaven granted come to curse me?"

sentences.zh: 俄而露復集，烏亦回翔。

translations.literal: Soon the dew gathered again, and the crow wheeled in flight once more.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the dew gathered anew, and the crow circled again on the wing.

sentences.zh: 詔作二闕於母墓前，又表其閭，蠲徭役，時號「闕下林家」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered two memorial arches built before his mother's tomb; his lane was also publicly honored and corvée labor exempted—the family was at the time called "the Lin household beneath the arches."
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded two memorial arches erected before his mother's tomb; his neighborhood was publicly honored as well, and corvée duties were remitted—at the time they were called "the Lin household beneath the arches."

sentences.zh: 陳饒奴，饒州人。

translations.literal: Chen Raonu was a native of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Raonu was from Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 年十二，親並亡，窶弱居喪，又歲饑，或教其分弟妹，可全性命。

translations.literal: At twelve, both parents were dead; destitute and weak in mourning, and with famine as well—some advised him to divide off his younger siblings so he might preserve his own life.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve both parents were gone; destitute, frail, and in mourning through a year of famine, some urged him to send his younger brother and sister away so he might save himself.

sentences.zh: 饒奴流涕，身丐訴相全養。

translations.literal: Raonu wept; going about in person, he begged and pleaded that they be kept and raised together.
translations.idiomatic: Raonu wept and went begging in person, pleading that all might be kept and raised together.

sentences.zh: 刺史李復異之，給資儲，署其門曰「孝友童子」。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Fu was struck by this and provided provisions; he inscribed his gate: "Filial-and-Fraternal Lad."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Fu marveled at this, supplied food and stores, and inscribed his gate: "The Filial-and-Fraternal Lad."

sentences.zh: 王博武，許州人。

translations.literal: Wang Bowu was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bowu was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，侍母至廣州，及沙湧口，暴風，母溺死，博武自投於水。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era, while attending his mother to Guangzhou, at Shayong Ford a sudden storm arose; his mother drowned, and Bowu cast himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang reign, while escorting his mother to Guangzhou, a sudden gale struck at Shayong Ford; his mother drowned, and Bowu threw himself into the water after her.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使盧貞俾吏沈罟，獲二屍焉，乃葬之，表其墓曰「孝子墓」。

translations.literal: The military governor of Lingnan, Lu Zhen, had clerks sink nets; both corpses were recovered, and they were buried; the tomb was publicly marked "Tomb of the Filial Son."
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan Military Governor Lu Zhen had his clerks lower nets into the water; both bodies were recovered and buried, and the grave was publicly marked "Tomb of the Filial Son."

sentences.zh: 詔為刻石。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a stone inscription carved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered stone carved to commemorate him.

sentences.zh: 萬敬儒，廬州人。

translations.literal: Wan Jingru was a native of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Jingru was from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 三世同居，喪親，廬墓，刺血寫浮屠書，斷手二指，輒復生。

translations.literal: Three generations dwelt together; when kin died he kept tomb vigil, pricked blood to copy Buddhist sutras, severed two fingers—and they grew back again.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations lived under one roof; when kin died he kept vigil at the tomb, pricked his blood to copy Buddhist scriptures, and severed two fingers—yet they grew back.

sentences.zh: 州改所居曰成孝鄉廣孝聚。

translations.literal: The prefecture renamed his district Chengxiao Village and Guangxiao Hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture renamed his home district Chengxiao Village and Guangxiao Hamlet.

sentences.zh: 大中時，表其家。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, his household was publicly honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong reign, his household was publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 章全益，梓州涪城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi was a native of Fucheng in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi was from Fucheng in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為兄全啟所鞠。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was reared by his elder brother Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his elder brother Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 母病，全啟刲股膳母而愈。

translations.literal: When their mother fell ill, Quanqi cut flesh from his thigh to feed her and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When their mother fell ill, Quanqi cut flesh from his thigh to feed her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 及全啟亡，全益服斬衰，斷手一指以報。

translations.literal: When Quanqi died, Quanyi wore the hemp mourning of the fiercest grade and severed one finger in recompense.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanqi died, Quanyi wore the deepest mourning and severed a finger in requital.

sentences.zh: 不畜妻，僮仆處一室，賣藥自業，世傳能作黃金。

translations.literal: He kept no wife; servants shared one room with him; he made his living selling medicine—folk lore held he could make gold.
translations.idiomatic: He took no wife; servants shared his single room; he earned his bread selling medicines—legend held he could transmute gold.

sentences.zh: 居成都四十年，號章孝子，卒，年九十八。

translations.literal: He lived in Chengdu forty years, styled Zhang the Filial Son; he died at ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in Chengdu forty years, known as Zhang the Filial Son; he died at ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：聖人治天下有道，曰「要在孝弟而已」。

translations.literal: Comment: The sage governs all under Heaven by a Way that runs, "All lies in filial piety and fraternal duty."
translations.idiomatic: Comment: The sage rules all under Heaven by a Way whose sum is this: "Everything turns on filial piety and brotherly duty."

sentences.zh: 父父也，子子也，兄兄也，弟弟也，推而之國，國而之天下，建一善而百行從，其失則以法繩之。

translations.literal: Father be father, son be son, elder brother elder brother, younger brother younger brother—extend this to the state, from the state to all under Heaven; establish one good and a hundred conduct follow; when there is failure, restrain it with law.
translations.idiomatic: Let the father be father, the son son, the elder brother elder brother, the younger brother younger brother—carry that from the household into the state, and from the state into the world; plant one goodness and a hundred deeds will follow; where men fail, bind them with law.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「孝者天下大本，法其末也。」

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "Filial piety is the great root of all under Heaven; law is its lesser branch."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Filial piety is the great root of the world; law is but its outer branch."

sentences.zh: 至匹夫單人，行孝一概，而兇盜不敢淩，天子喟而旌之者，以其教孝而求忠也。

translations.literal: Down to a single common man practicing filial piety in one fashion, violent robbers dare not assault him; when the Son of Heaven sighs and honors such men, it is because through teaching filial piety he seeks loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a lone commoner practices filial piety in a single steadfast way, violent robbers dare not molest him; when the Son of Heaven sighs and honors such men, it is because in teaching filial piety he seeks loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故裒而著於篇。

translations.literal: Therefore these accounts are gathered and set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore these lives are gathered and recorded in this chapter.
